title.raw: 卷二百七十四 列傳第三十三 王贊 張保續 趙玭 盧懷忠 王繼勳 丁德裕 張延通 梁迥 史珪 田欽祚 侯贇 王文寶 翟守素 王侁 劉審瓊 Volume 274 Biographies 33: Wang Zan, Zhang Baoxu, Zhao Pin, Lu Huaizhong, Wang Jixun, Ding Deyu, Zhang Yantong, Liang Jiong, Shi Gui, Tian Qinzuo, Hou Yun, Wang Wenbao, Di Shousu, Wang Shen, Liu Shenqiong

sentences.zh: 建隆初，始平李重進，太祖素知贊材幹，可委以完葺，即令知揚州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianlong, when Li Chongjin was first pacified, Taizu had long known Zan's talent and capability and that he could be entrusted with complete restoration; he immediately appointed him to administer Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianlong reign, after Li Chongjin's rebellion was first put down, Emperor Taizu had long recognized Wang Zan's ability and judged him fit to oversee full reconstruction; he promptly made him prefect of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 既行，舟覆於閶橋下，溺死，親屬隨沒者三人。

translations.literal: After he had set out, his boat capsized beneath Chang Bridge; he drowned, and three relatives who accompanied him also perished.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly after he departed, his boat overturned below Chang Bridge; he drowned, and three kinsmen traveling with him were lost as well.

sentences.zh: 上甚嗟悼，謂左右曰：「溺吾樞密使矣！」

translations.literal: The emperor deeply mourned and lamented, saying to those around him, "I have drowned my Privy Councilor!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor grieved deeply and said to his attendants, "I have drowned my Privy Councilor!"

sentences.zh: 蓋將大用也。

translations.literal: He had evidently been about to receive great employment.
translations.idiomatic: —for he had clearly been on the verge of major promotion.

sentences.zh: 賻其家絹三百匹，米、麥各二百斛。

translations.literal: Funeral gifts to his family were three hundred bolts of silk, and two hundred hu each of rice and wheat.
translations.idiomatic: His family received three hundred bolts of silk in condolence gifts, along with two hundred hu of rice and two hundred hu of wheat.

sentences.zh: 張保續

translations.literal: Zhang Baoxu
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Baoxu

sentences.zh: 張保續，字嗣光，京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: Zhang Baoxu, courtesy name Siguang, was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Baoxu, whose courtesy name was Siguang, came from Wannian in the Jingzhao region.

sentences.zh: 父洪，唐左武衛上將軍，保續以蔭補太廟齋郎。

translations.literal: His father Hong was Tang Left Martial Guard senior general; Baoxu entered service by yin privilege as Grand Temple Aide.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhang Hong had been a senior general of the Tang Left Martial Guard; Baoxu received an initial appointment as Grand Temple Aide through his father's privilege.

sentences.zh: 梁貞明中，調補臨濟尉，選充四方館通事舍人。

translations.literal: In the middle of Liang Zhenming, he was transferred to fill the post of Linji commandant and selected to serve as Sifang Guan communications attendant.
translations.idiomatic: During the Liang Zhenming era he was reassigned as commandant of Linji and then chosen to serve as a communications attendant at the Office of Foreign Affairs.

sentences.zh: 後唐天成初，領瓜州官告國信副使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Later Tang Tiancheng, he headed the Guazhou credential imperial envoy deputy mission.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Later Tang Tiancheng reign he served as deputy envoy on the imperial credential mission to Guazhou.

sentences.zh: 郊祀，改右贊善大夫。

translations.literal: At the suburban sacrifice, he was changed to Right Assistant in the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: After the suburban sacrifice he was promoted to Right Assistant in the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 晉天福中，歷太府、光祿二少卿，職同正，領通事舍人。

translations.literal: In Jin Tianfu, he successively held the two junior minister posts of Grand Treasury and Director of Imperial Entertainments, with duties equal to the full rank, and headed the communications attendant post.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jin Tianfu period he served in succession as junior minister of the Grand Treasury and of the Directorate of Imperial Entertainments, with duties equivalent to the full ministers, while also retaining his post as communications attendant.

sentences.zh: 開運二年，契丹入寇，杜重威、李守貞、符彥卿等率兵禦之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaiyun, the Khitan invaded; Du Chongwei, Li Shouzhen, Fu Yanqing, and others led troops to resist them.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaiyun the Khitan invaded, and Du Chongwei, Li Shouzhen, Fu Yanqing, and others led armies to meet them.

sentences.zh: 命保續馳騎往來軍中諭機事。

translations.literal: Baoxu was ordered to ride swiftly back and forth through the armies to convey strategic matters.
translations.idiomatic: Baoxu was ordered to ride between the armies and relay operational instructions.

sentences.zh: 既而大破敵於陽城，使還，以本官充西上閤門副使。

translations.literal: Thereafter the enemy was greatly defeated at Yangcheng; on his return he was appointed with his original rank as Western Upper Gate deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the enemy suffered a major defeat at Yangcheng; when he returned he was appointed Western Upper Gate deputy commissioner at his existing rank.

sentences.zh: 明年，使荊南，復命轉東上閤門副使。

translations.literal: The next year he was envoy to Jingnan; on his return he was transferred to Eastern Upper Gate deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was sent on a mission to Jingnan, and on his return was transferred to Eastern Upper Gate deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 契丹犯闕，被驅北徙，留范陽，歲餘逃歸。

translations.literal: When the Khitan violated the capital, he was driven north in relocation, remained at Fanyang, and after more than a year fled back.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan seized the capital he was forced north with the court, remained at Fanyang for over a year, and then escaped back to the south.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐初，出為隴州防禦使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han Qianyou, he went out as Longzhou defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Later Han Qianyou reign he was appointed defense commissioner of Longzhou.

sentences.zh: 周祖革命，召為東上閤門副使，從平慕容彥超。

translations.literal: When Zhou Taizu carried out the revolution, he was summoned as Eastern Upper Gate deputy commissioner and followed in pacifying Murong Yanchao.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong of Later Zhou seized power, Baoxu was recalled as Eastern Upper Gate deputy commissioner and took part in suppressing Murong Yanchao.

sentences.zh: 累遷引進副使、知閤門事。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Reception deputy commissioner and overseer of gate affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to Reception deputy commissioner and supervisor of gate protocol.

sentences.zh: 世宗即位，授西上閤門使。

translations.literal: When Shizong took the throne, he was granted Western Upper Gate commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Shizong acceded, he was appointed Western Upper Gate commissioner.

sentences.zh: 明年，進秩東上閤門使。

translations.literal: The next year his rank advanced to Eastern Upper Gate commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was promoted to Eastern Upper Gate commissioner.

sentences.zh: 從上征淮南，會壽州納款，遣保續先往慰撫，及劉仁贍率將卒出降，以功遷判四方館事，就遷客省使。

translations.literal: He followed the emperor on the Huainan campaign; when Shouzhou submitted, Baoxu was sent ahead to comfort and reassure; when Liu Renzhan led officers and soldiers out to surrender, for merit he was moved to oversee Sifang Guan affairs and then promoted to guest-relations commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor on the campaign against Huainan; when Shouzhou surrendered he was sent ahead to reassure the populace, and after Liu Renzhan led his troops out to submit he was rewarded with oversight of the Office of Foreign Affairs and soon after with the post of guest-relations commissioner.

sentences.zh: 從平瓦橋關，奉使吳越。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying Waqiao Pass and was sent on mission to Wu-Yue.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the pacification of Waqiao Pass and was then dispatched on a mission to Wu-Yue.

sentences.zh: 宋初，遷衛尉卿，判四方館、客省、閤門事。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, he was moved to Commandant of the Guards and concurrently judged Sifang Guan, guest-relations, and gate affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he was promoted to Commandant of the Guards while concurrently overseeing the Office of Foreign Affairs, the guest-relations office, and gate protocol.

sentences.zh: 保續性介直，好儉素，在閤門前後四十年，善宣贊辭，令聽者傾聳。

translations.literal: Baoxu's nature was upright and direct; he loved plain thrift; for some forty years before and after in the gate office he excelled at proclaiming eulogistic phrases, making listeners lean forward in awe.
translations.idiomatic: Baoxu was upright and frugal by nature; he spent roughly forty years in gate service, where his ceremonial announcements were so compelling that listeners would straighten in attentive awe.

sentences.zh: 累使藩國不辱命。

translations.literal: Repeated missions to feudatory states never dishonored his charge.
translations.idiomatic: On repeated missions to vassal states he never failed in his charge.

sentences.zh: 歷事六朝，未嘗有過。

translations.literal: Serving through six dynasties, he never once had a fault.
translations.idiomatic: He served six successive dynasties without a single recorded lapse.

sentences.zh: 從征李筠，以足疾留河內，後歸京師。

translations.literal: On the campaign against Li Jun he remained at Henei because of foot ailment, and later returned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Li Jun he was left at Henei because of a foot ailment and later returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 建隆三年，卒，年六十四。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianlong he died, aged sixty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Jianlong, at the age of sixty-four.

sentences.zh: 趙玭，澶州人。

translations.literal: Zhao Pin, a man of Danzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Pin was a native of Danzhou.

sentences.zh: 家富於財。

translations.literal: His family was rich in wealth.
translations.idiomatic: His family was wealthy.

sentences.zh: 晉天福中，以納粟助邊用，補集賢小史，調濮州司戶參軍。

translations.literal: In Jin Tianfu, by presenting grain to aid frontier expenses he was given a supplemental post as Junior Archivist of the Hall of Assembled Worthies and was transferred to Puzhou revenue adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jin Tianfu period he contributed grain to support frontier expenses and received a supplemental post in the Hall of Assembled Worthies, then was assigned as revenue adjutant in Puzhou.

sentences.zh: 刺史白重進以其年少，欲試以事，因以滯獄授之。

translations.literal: Prefect Bai Chongjin, because he was young, wished to test him with affairs and therefore handed over to him stagnant prison cases.
translations.idiomatic: Because he was young, Prefect Bai Chongjin wished to test his ability and therefore assigned him the backlog of stalled court cases.

sentences.zh: 玭為平決，悉能中理。

translations.literal: Pin adjudicated and settled them; all could hit the principle.
translations.idiomatic: Pin cleared and decided them all, and in every case his judgments were sound.

sentences.zh: 重進移刺虢、成二州，連辟為從事。

translations.literal: Chongjin moved to govern the two prefectures of Guo and Cheng and repeatedly summoned him as staff officer.
translations.idiomatic: When Chongjin was transferred to govern Guo and Cheng prefectures he repeatedly recruited Pin as a staff officer.

sentences.zh: 會契丹構難，秦帥何重建獻地於蜀，孟知祥署高彥儔秦州節度，成為支郡，因署玭秦、成、階等州觀察判官。

translations.literal: When the Khitan stirred trouble, Qin commander He Chongjian presented territory to Shu; Meng Zhixiang appointed Gao Yanchou Qinzhou military commissioner, with Cheng as a subordinate prefecture, and therefore appointed Pin observation judge for Qin, Cheng, Jie, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan stirred up trouble, the Qin commander He Chongjian surrendered his territory to Shu; Meng Zhixiang appointed Gao Yanchou military commissioner of Qinzhou, with Cheng as a subordinate prefecture, and made Pin observation judge for Qin, Cheng, Jie, and related prefectures.

sentences.zh: 周顯德初，命王景帥兵討秦鳳。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhou Xiande, Wang Jing was ordered to lead troops to campaign against Qin and Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Zhou Xiande reign Wang Jing was ordered to lead an army against Qin and Feng.

sentences.zh: 彥儔出兵救援，未至，聞軍敗，因潰歸。

translations.literal: Yanchou led troops out to rescue; before arriving he heard the army had been defeated and therefore scattered in flight back.
translations.idiomatic: Yanchou marched out to relieve them, but before he arrived he heard the army had been defeated and fled back in disarray.

sentences.zh: 玭閉門不納，召官屬諭之曰：「今中朝兵甲無敵於天下，自用師西征，戰無不勝。

translations.literal: Pin closed the gates and would not admit him, summoned officials and instructed them, saying, "Now the central court's arms and armor are unmatched under Heaven; since troops were sent west on campaign, in battle there has been no defeat.
translations.idiomatic: Pin shut the gates and refused him entry, then summoned the officials and said, "The central court's armies are now unmatched in the realm; since the western campaign began they have won every battle.

sentences.zh: 蜀中所遣，將皆武勇者，卒皆驍銳者，然殺戮遁逃之外，幾無孑遺。

translations.literal: Those Shu sent out—all generals were martial and brave, all soldiers fierce and sharp—yet apart from slaughter and flight, almost none were left surviving.
translations.idiomatic: The forces Shu has sent—all their commanders were fierce warriors and all their troops elite fighters—yet apart from the killed and the fugitives, scarcely a man has returned.

sentences.zh: 我輩安忍坐受其禍？

translations.literal: How can we bear to sit and receive this calamity?
translations.idiomatic: How can we sit still and invite such disaster upon ourselves?

sentences.zh: 去危就安，當在今日。」

translations.literal: Leaving danger and approaching safety should be today."
translations.idiomatic: To leave danger for safety—we must act today."

sentences.zh: 眾皆俯伏聽命。

translations.literal: All bowed low and listened to his orders.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone bowed low and accepted his command.

sentences.zh: 玭遂以城歸朝。

translations.literal: Pin thereupon surrendered the city to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Pin then surrendered the city to the central court.

sentences.zh: 世宗欲命以藩鎮，宰相范質不可，乃授郢州刺史，歷汝、密、澤三州刺史。

translations.literal: Shizong wished to appoint him to a frontier command; Chancellor Fan Zhi objected, and he was therefore granted Ezhou prefect and successively served as prefect of Ru, Mi, and Ze.
translations.idiomatic: Shizong wished to give him a military governorship, but Chancellor Fan Zhi opposed it; he was instead appointed prefect of Ezhou and later served in succession as prefect of Ru, Mi, and Ze.

sentences.zh: 建隆中，入為宗正卿。

translations.literal: In Jianlong he entered the capital as Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jianlong reign he was recalled to the capital as Director of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 乾德初，出為泰州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qiande he went out as Taizhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qiande reign he was appointed prefect of Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 二年，改左監門衛大將軍、判三司。

translations.literal: In the second year he was changed to Left Gate Guard senior general and judged the Three Departments.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was made senior general of the Left Gate Guard and placed in charge of the Three Departments.

sentences.zh: 玭狂躁婞直，多忤上旨，太祖頗優容之。

translations.literal: Pin was wild, rash, obstinate, and straight; he often offended imperial intent, yet Taizu was quite indulgent toward him.
translations.idiomatic: Pin was impulsive, blunt, and obstinate, and often ran counter to the emperor's wishes, yet Taizu treated him with considerable forbearance.

sentences.zh: 嘗廉得宰相趙普私市秦、隴大木事，潛以奏白，然懼普知，因稱足疾求解職。

translations.literal: He once investigated and obtained evidence that Chancellor Zhao Pu privately marketed great timber from Qin and Long, secretly reported it to inform the throne, yet feared Pu would learn of it and therefore claimed foot ailment to request release from office.
translations.idiomatic: He once uncovered evidence that Chancellor Zhao Pu had been privately trading large timber from Qin and Long, reported it secretly to the throne, but fearing that Pu would find out he pleaded foot ailment and asked to resign his post.

sentences.zh: 五年春，罷使，守本官。

translations.literal: In spring of the fifth year his envoy duties were ended; he kept his original office.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fifth year he was relieved of his special assignment and retained only his base rank.

sentences.zh: 自是累獻密疏，皆留中不出，常疑普中傷。

translations.literal: From then on he repeatedly submitted secret memorials, all kept within and not issued; he constantly suspected Pu of slandering him.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter he repeatedly submitted confidential memorials, all of which were kept within and never acted upon; he constantly suspected that Pu was working against him behind the scenes.

sentences.zh: 六年，詣闕，納所授告命，詔勒歸私第。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he came to court, surrendered the commission he had received, and was ordered by edict to return to his private residence.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he came to court, surrendered his commission of appointment, and was ordered by edict to return to his private residence.

sentences.zh: 又請退居鄆州，不許。

translations.literal: He again requested to retire and dwell at Yanzhou; this was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: He also asked permission to retire to Yanzhou, but the request was denied.

sentences.zh: 玭不勝忿，踰年，伺普入朝，馬前揚言其短。

translations.literal: Pin could not overcome his rage; after more than a year he waited until Pu entered court and before his horse publicly proclaimed his faults.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to contain his anger, Pin waited more than a year until Pu was entering court and then shouted out his faults in front of Pu's horse.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，召玭及普於便殿，面質其事。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it, he summoned Pin and Pu to the informal hall and confronted them face to face on the matter.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this he summoned Pin and Pu to the informal hall and confronted them directly about the affair.

sentences.zh: 玭大言詆普販木規利，上怒，促令集百官逐普，且諭其事。

translations.literal: Pin spoke loudly slandering Pu for trafficking timber to seek profit; the emperor was angry and urgently ordered the assembly of all officials to expel Pu, also instructing them on the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Pin loudly accused Pu of trading timber for private gain; the emperor flew into a rage and urgently ordered all officials assembled to drive Pu from office, explaining the charges to them.

sentences.zh: 王溥等奏玭誣罔大臣，普事得解。

translations.literal: Wang Pu and others memorialized that Pin had falsely accused a great minister; Pu's affair was resolved.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Pu and others reported that Pin had falsely accused a senior minister, and the case against Pu was dropped.

sentences.zh: 上詰責玭，命武士撾之，令御史鞫於殿庭。

translations.literal: The emperor interrogated and reproached Pin, ordered warriors to beat him with rods, and commanded the censor to examine him in the palace courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rebuked Pin, ordered guards to beat him with rods, and had the censor try his case in the palace courtyard.

sentences.zh: 普為營救，得寬其罰，黜為汝州牙校。

translations.literal: Pu worked to rescue him; his punishment was leniently reduced and he was demoted to Ruzhou military adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: Pu intervened on his behalf, and his punishment was lightened to demotion as a military adjutant in Ruzhou.

sentences.zh: 太平興國三年卒，年五十八。

translations.literal: He died in the third year of Taiping Xingguo, aged fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year of Taiping Xingguo, at the age of fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 盧懷忠

translations.literal: Lu Huaizhong
translations.idiomatic: Lu Huaizhong

sentences.zh: 盧懷忠，瀛州河間人。

translations.literal: Lu Huaizhong, a native of Hejian in Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Huaizhong was a native of Hejian in Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 少有膂力，善騎射。

translations.literal: In youth he had physical strength and excelled at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he was powerfully built and skilled in horsemanship and archery.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐初，寓居河中，值李守貞之叛，周祖圍其城，懷忠夜踰城出見，陳攻取便宜。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han Qianyou he resided at Hedong; when Li Shouzhen rebelled and Zhou Taizu besieged his city, Huaizhong by night climbed over the wall to go out and meet him, presenting advantageous plans for attack and capture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Later Han Qianyou reign he was living in Hedong when Li Shouzhen rebelled; as Zhou Taizu besieged the city, Huaizhong climbed over the wall by night to meet him and offered practical advice on how to take it.

sentences.zh: 河中平，奏補供奉官。

translations.literal: When Hedong was pacified, he was memorialized for appointment as palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: After Hedong was pacified he was recommended for appointment as a palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 從征慕容彥超於兗州。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Murong Yanchao at Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the campaign against Murong Yanchao at Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 顯德初，監沂州軍，以所部破海州，功居多。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiande he supervised Yizhou forces; with his command he broke Haizhou, and his merit was foremost.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Xiande reign he supervised the army at Yizhou; his troops captured Haizhou, and he earned the lion's share of the credit.

sentences.zh: 世宗議北征，先遣懷忠按視出師道路。

translations.literal: When Shizong deliberated the northern expedition, he first sent Huaizhong to inspect and survey the army's route of march.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong planned the northern campaign he first sent Huaizhong to reconnoiter the army's line of march.

sentences.zh: 三關平，遷如京副使。

translations.literal: When the Three Passes were pacified, he was moved to Capital Reception deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After the Three Passes were pacified he was promoted to Capital Reception deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 宋初，遷內酒坊副使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was moved to Inner Wine Workshop deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he was appointed deputy commissioner of the Inner Wine Workshop.

sentences.zh: 會朗州軍亂，太祖將出師致討，遣懷忠使荊南，因謂曰：「江陵人情去就，山川向背，我欲盡知之。」

translations.literal: When Langzhou troops rebelled and Taizu was about to lead troops out to punish them, he sent Huaizhong as envoy to Jingnan and therefore said to him, "The people's inclinations in Jiangling, whether to stay or go, and the mountains and rivers facing toward or away—I wish to know all of it thoroughly."
translations.idiomatic: When the army at Langzhou mutinied and Taizu prepared to march out against them, he sent Huaizhong on a mission to Jingnan and told him, "I want to know everything about Jiangling—the people's loyalties, the lay of the land, which routes favor attack and which do not."

sentences.zh: 懷忠使還，奏曰：「繼沖甲兵雖整，而控弦不過三萬；

translations.literal: When Huaizhong returned from his mission he memorialized, saying, "Jichong's armor and weapons are though orderly, yet bowmen under his command are no more than thirty thousand;
translations.idiomatic: When Huaizhong returned he reported, "Jichong's forces are well equipped, but he has no more than thirty thousand archers under arms;

sentences.zh: 年穀雖登，而民苦於暴斂。

translations.literal: though the year's grain harvest was abundant, the people suffered under violent exactions.
translations.idiomatic: although the harvest was good, the people are ground down by harsh levies.

sentences.zh: 南邇長沙，東距金陵，西迫巴蜀，北奉朝廷。

translations.literal: To the south it adjoins Changsha, to the east it faces off against Jinling, to the west it is pressed by Ba-Shu, and to the north it must serve the court.
translations.idiomatic: To the south lies Changsha, to the east Jinling blocks the way, to the west Ba-Shu presses in, and to the north it must answer to the court.

sentences.zh: 觀其形勢，蓋日不暇給矣。」

translations.literal: Observing its strategic posture, it can scarcely attend to each day."
translations.idiomatic: Judging by its strategic position, the regime can barely keep its head above water."

sentences.zh: 太祖召宰相范質等謂曰：「江陵四分五裂之國，今出師湖南，假道荊渚，因而下之，萬全策也。」

translations.literal: Taizu summoned Chancellor Fan Zhi and others and said, "Jiangling is a state split four and five ways; now to send troops to Hunan, borrow the road through Jingzhu, and thereby bring it down is a plan of ten thousand completeness."
translations.idiomatic: Taizu summoned Chancellor Fan Zhi and the others and said, "Jiangling is a realm already torn apart; if we march on Hunan now and borrow the route through Jingzhou to bring it down as well, that is the surest plan."

sentences.zh: 即以懷忠為前軍步軍都監。

translations.literal: He thereupon appointed Huaizhong vanguard infantry army overseer.
translations.idiomatic: He then appointed Huaizhong overseer of the vanguard infantry.

sentences.zh: 荊湖平，以功遷內酒坊使。

translations.literal: When Jing and Hu were pacified, for merit he was moved to Inner Wine Workshop commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After Jing and Hu were pacified he was promoted to commissioner of the Inner Wine Workshop for his service.

sentences.zh: 乾德二年，改判四方館事，知江陵府。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qiande he was changed to judge Sifang Guan affairs and administer Jiangling prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qiande he was placed in charge of the Office of Foreign Affairs while serving as prefect of Jiangling.

sentences.zh: 四年，王師伐蜀。

translations.literal: In the fourth year the imperial army campaigned against Shu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year the imperial army marched against Shu.

sentences.zh: 江陵當峽、江會衝，以供億之勞，遷客省使。

translations.literal: Jiangling stood at the junction of the Gorges and the Yangzi; for the labor of supplying provisions he was moved to guest-relations commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Because Jiangling lay at the junction of the Gorges and the Yangzi and bore the burden of supplying the campaign, he was transferred to guest-relations commissioner.

sentences.zh: 又明年，使江南還，中途遇疾，肩輿歸京師。

translations.literal: The next year again, returning from a mission to Jiangnan, he fell ill en route and was carried in a sedan chair back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, while returning from a mission to Jiangnan, he fell ill on the road and was carried back to the capital in a sedan chair.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣醫丸艾以賜之，未幾卒，年四十九。

translations.literal: Taizu sent physicians with pills and moxibustion as gifts to him; before long he died, aged forty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu sent physicians with medicines and moxibustion supplies as gifts, but he died soon afterward, at the age of forty-nine.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符四年，錄其子熙為校書郎。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Dazhong Xiangfu his son Xi was recorded and appointed collator.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Dazhong Xiangfu his son Xi was granted appointment as collator.

sentences.zh: 王繼勳

translations.literal: Wang Jixun
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jixun

sentences.zh: 王繼勳，陝州平陸人。

translations.literal: Wang Jixun, a native of Pinglu in Shaanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jixun was a native of Pinglu in Shaanzhou.

sentences.zh: 隸河中府為牙校。

translations.literal: He was attached to Hedong prefecture as military adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: He served as a military adjutant in Hedong prefecture.

sentences.zh: 李守貞之叛，令繼勳據潼關，為郭從義所破，走還河中。

translations.literal: When Li Shouzhen rebelled, he ordered Jixun to hold Tong Pass; he was broken by Guo Congyi and fled back to Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: During Li Shouzhen's rebellion he was ordered to hold Tong Pass; Guo Congyi defeated him and he fled back to Hedong.

sentences.zh: 俄白文珂、劉詞領兵至城下，守貞又遣繼勳與其愛將聶知遇夜出攻河西砦，復為漢兵所敗，被創而遁。

translations.literal: Soon Bai Wenke and Liu Ci led troops to the foot of the city; Shouzhen again sent Jixun with his favorite general Nie Zhiyu by night to attack the Hexi stockade, and again they were defeated by Han troops; wounded, he fled.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Bai Wenke and Liu Ci brought their armies to the city walls; Shouzhen again sent Jixun with his favorite general Nie Zhiyu to attack the stockade west of the river by night, but Han forces defeated them again and Jixun escaped wounded.

sentences.zh: 繼勳度守貞必敗，遂踰城出降，周祖奏補供奉官。

translations.literal: Jixun judged that Shouzhen must be defeated and therefore climbed over the wall to surrender; Zhou Taizu memorialized him for appointment as palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Jixun concluded that Shouzhen was doomed, climbed over the wall to surrender, and Zhou Taizu recommended him for appointment as palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 廣順初，領汾州刺史，充晉、磁、隰等州緣邊巡檢，歷憲、麟、石、磁四州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Guangshun he headed Fenzhou prefect and served as frontier inspector for Jin, Ci, Xi, and other prefectures, and successively held the four prefectures of Xian, Lin, Shi, and Ci.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Guangshun reign he served as prefect of Fenzhou and as frontier inspector for Jin, Ci, Xi, and neighboring prefectures, and later governed in succession the prefectures of Xian, Lin, Shi, and Ci.

sentences.zh: 宋初，遷磁州團練使，坐境上用兵失律、荊罕儒陷陣，責授右監門衛率。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was moved to Cizhou regimentation commissioner; for using troops within his jurisdiction in violation of regulations and Jing Hanru falling in battle he was punished and appointed Right Gate Guard colonel.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he was made regimentation commissioner of Cizhou; because he had violated regulations in deploying troops within his jurisdiction and Jing Hanru had been killed in battle, he was demoted to colonel of the Right Gate Guard.

sentences.zh: 初平荊襄，命權知道州，未幾，授本州刺史。

translations.literal: When Jing and Xiang were first pacified, he was ordered to act as Daozhou prefect; before long he was granted prefect of that prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing and Xiang were first pacified he was appointed acting prefect of Daozhou and soon after confirmed in that post.

sentences.zh: 州境與廣南接，劉鋹屢引兵入寇，繼勳因上言嶺表可圖之狀。

translations.literal: The prefecture's territory adjoined Guangnan; Liu Chang repeatedly led troops in to raid, and Jixun therefore submitted a report on how the Lingnan region could be targeted.
translations.idiomatic: His prefecture bordered Guangnan, and Liu Chang repeatedly led raids across the border; Jixun therefore submitted a memorial on how the Lingnan region might be conquered.

sentences.zh: 及王師南伐，以為賀州道行營馬步軍都監。

translations.literal: When the imperial army campaigned south, he was made Hezhou route campaign army cavalry and infantry overseer.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army marched south he was appointed overseer of cavalry and infantry on the Hezhou campaign route.

sentences.zh: 繼勳有武勇，在軍陣，常用鐵鞭、鐵槊、鐵楇，軍中目為「王三鐵」。

translations.literal: Jixun had martial valor; in battle arrays he commonly used iron whip, iron spear, and iron mace; in the army he was styled "Wang Three Irons."
translations.idiomatic: Jixun was a fierce fighter; in battle he habitually wielded an iron whip, iron spear, and iron mace, and the troops called him "Wang Three Irons."

sentences.zh: 丁德裕

translations.literal: Ding Deyu
translations.idiomatic: Ding Deyu

sentences.zh: 丁德裕，洺州臨洺人。

translations.literal: Ding Deyu, a native of Linming in Mingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Deyu was a native of Linming in Mingzhou.

sentences.zh: 父審琦，彰武軍節度。

translations.literal: His father Shenqi was Zhangwu Army military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ding Shenqi was military commissioner of the Zhangwu Army.

sentences.zh: 周廣順初，以蔭補供奉官。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhou Guangshun, by yin privilege he was given supplemental appointment as palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Later Zhou Guangshun reign he entered service as a palace attendant through his father's privilege.

sentences.zh: 宋初，歷通事舍人、西上閤門副使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he successively served as communications attendant and Western Upper Gate deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he served in succession as communications attendant and Western Upper Gate deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 建隆三年，遷東上閤門使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Jianlong he was moved to Eastern Upper Gate commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Jianlong he was promoted to Eastern Upper Gate commissioner.

sentences.zh: 從慕容延釗平荊湖，以功授引進使。

translations.literal: He followed Murong Yanzhou in pacifying Jing and Hu and for merit was granted Reception commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in Murong Yanzhou's pacification of Jing and Hu and was appointed Reception commissioner for his service.

sentences.zh: 又與潘美、尹崇珂克郴州，遷客省使。

translations.literal: Again with Pan Mei and Yin Chongke he captured Chenzhou and was moved to guest-relations commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Pan Mei and Yin Chongke in capturing Chenzhou and was promoted to guest-relations commissioner.

sentences.zh: 乾德五年，遷內客省使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Qiande he was moved to Inner Guest Relations commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Qiande he was made Inner Guest Relations commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時成都初平，群寇大起，用為西川都巡檢使，與閤門副使張延通同率師討之，擒賊帥康祚，磔於市。

translations.literal: At that time Chengdu had just been pacified and bandits rose in great numbers; he was employed as Xichuan chief inspector and together with gate deputy commissioner Zhang Yantong led troops to campaign against them, captured the bandit leader Kang Zuo, and dismembered him in the market.
translations.idiomatic: When Chengdu had only recently been pacified and banditry flared across the region, he was appointed chief inspector of Xichuan; he and gate deputy commissioner Zhang Yantong led troops against the rebels, captured the bandit chief Kang Zuo, and had him torn apart in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，盡平其黨。

translations.literal: After more than a year, their faction was entirely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year he had eliminated their entire faction.

sentences.zh: 頗與延通不協，歸朝，告其陰事，延通坐棄市。

translations.literal: He was quite at odds with Yantong; returning to court he reported his secret affairs, and Yantong was punished with execution in the market.
translations.idiomatic: He had fallen out badly with Yantong; on returning to court he denounced Yantong's secret misconduct, and Yantong was executed in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 又奏轉運使、禮部郎中李鉉嘗醉酒，言涉指斥。

translations.literal: He again memorialized that transport commissioner and Ministry of Rites bureau director Li Xuan had once been drunk and his words touched on denunciation.
translations.idiomatic: He also reported that transport commissioner and Ministry of Rites bureau director Li Xuan had once spoken seditiously while drunk.

sentences.zh: 上怒，驛召鉉下御史案之。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and by relay summoned Xuan down to the censorate to investigate the case.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and ordered Li Xuan brought back by courier to face investigation by the censorate.

sentences.zh: 鉉言德裕在蜀日屢以事請求，多拒之，皆有狀。

translations.literal: Xuan said that during Deyu's days in Shu he had repeatedly made requests on various matters and Xuan had mostly refused them, all with documented grounds.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xuan replied that while Deyu was in Shu he had repeatedly made improper requests, most of which Xuan had refused—and he had records to prove it.

sentences.zh: 御史以聞。

translations.literal: The censorate reported it to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: The censorate reported this to the throne.

sentences.zh: 太祖悟，止坐鉉酒失，責授左贊善大夫。

translations.literal: Taizu understood; he only punished Xuan for the wine offense and demoted him to Left Assistant in the Palace Library.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu saw through the affair, punished Li Xuan only for his drunken lapse, and demoted him to Left Assistant in the Palace Library.

sentences.zh: 未幾，德裕亦出知潞州。

translations.literal: Before long Deyu also went out to administer Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Deyu was also sent out to serve as prefect of Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 會征江南，遣德裕為常州行營兵馬都監，領吳越兵，助主帥進討。

translations.literal: When the campaign against Jiangnan arose, Deyu was sent as Changzhou campaign army cavalry and infantry overseer, leading Wu-Yue troops to assist the commander in advancing the attack.
translations.idiomatic: During the campaign against Jiangnan he was appointed overseer of cavalry and infantry on the Changzhou campaign route, commanding Wu-Yue troops to support the main force.

sentences.zh: 常州平，命權知州事。

translations.literal: When Changzhou was pacified, he was ordered to act as administrator of prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Changzhou fell he was appointed acting prefect.

sentences.zh: 又改昇州東南路行營都監，敗潤州軍五千餘於城下。

translations.literal: He was again changed to Shenzhou Southeastern Route campaign overseer and defeated more than five thousand Runzhou troops beneath the city walls.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made overseer of the Shenzhou Southeastern Route campaign and defeated more than five thousand Runzhou troops below the city walls.

sentences.zh: 及拔潤州，移領常、潤等州經略巡檢使。

translations.literal: When Runzhou was taken, he was moved to head the strategic inspector for Chang, Run, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: After Runzhou was captured he was placed in charge of strategic inspection for Chang, Run, and neighboring prefectures.

sentences.zh: 德裕以傾險為眾所惡，恃勢剛狠，不恤士卒，黷貨無厭，越人苦之。

translations.literal: Deyu was hated by the multitude for his treacherous scheming; relying on power he was harsh and cruel, showed no care for soldiers, and was insatiable in corrupt exactions, and the Yue people suffered bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu was widely hated for his treachery; he abused his authority with brutal harshness, neglected his troops, and extorted bribes without end, and the people of Yue suffered under him.

sentences.zh: 錢俶奏其事，貶房州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: Qian Chu memorialized on the matter; he was demoted to Fangzhou prefect and died.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Chu reported his conduct to the throne; Deyu was demoted to prefect of Fangzhou, where he died.

sentences.zh: 張延通

translations.literal: Zhang Yantong
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yantong

sentences.zh: 張延通，潞州潞城人。

translations.literal: Zhang Yantong, a native of Lucheng in Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yantong was a native of Lucheng in Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 父彥成，周右金吾衛上將軍。

translations.literal: His father Yancheng was Zhou Right Golden Crow Guard senior general.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhang Yancheng had been a senior general of the Later Zhou Right Golden Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 延通性穎悟，有才幹，蔭補供奉官。

translations.literal: Yantong's nature was quick and perceptive; he had talent and capability and entered by yin privilege as palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Yantong was quick-witted and capable; he entered service as a palace attendant through his father's privilege.

sentences.zh: 宋初，歷通事舍人，遷東上閤門副使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he served as communications attendant and was moved to Eastern Upper Gate deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song he served as communications attendant and was promoted to Eastern Upper Gate deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 開寶中，為西川兵馬都監。

translations.literal: In Kaibao he was Xichuan army cavalry and infantry overseer.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaibao reign he served as overseer of cavalry and infantry in Xichuan.

sentences.zh: 太祖以蜀寇未平，命同內客省使丁德裕、引進副使王班、內臣張嶼領兵屯蜀部。

translations.literal: Taizu, because Shu bandits were not yet pacified, ordered him together with Inner Guest Relations commissioner Ding Deyu, Reception deputy commissioner Wang Ban, and inner attendant Zhang Yu to lead troops stationed in the Shu region.
translations.idiomatic: Because banditry in Shu had not yet been suppressed, Taizu ordered him to join Inner Guest Relations commissioner Ding Deyu, Reception deputy commissioner Wang Ban, and inner attendant Zhang Yu in garrisoning troops in the Shu region.

sentences.zh: 德裕頗專恣，延通面質其短，德裕銜之。

translations.literal: Deyu was quite arbitrary and willful; Yantong confronted him to his face with his faults, and Deyu harbored resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu was domineering and arbitrary; Yantong confronted him openly about his misconduct, and Deyu bore a grudge.

sentences.zh: 又與張嶼不協，延通亦為和解之，德裕疑延通與嶼為黨，益不悅。

translations.literal: He was again at odds with Zhang Yu; Yantong also worked to reconcile them, but Deyu suspected Yantong and Yu were a faction and was all the more displeased.
translations.idiomatic: He also clashed with Zhang Yu; Yantong tried to mediate between them, but Deyu suspected Yantong and Yu were in league and grew even more hostile.

sentences.zh: 會太祖征太原，有使自行在至，備言太祖當盛暑躬冒矢石，勞頓萬狀。

translations.literal: When Taizu campaigned against Taiyuan, an envoy came from the imperial camp and fully described how Taizu in the height of summer personally braved arrows and stones, exhausted in ten thousand ways.
translations.idiomatic: During Taizu's campaign against Taiyuan an envoy arrived from headquarters reporting that the emperor, in the height of summer, was personally braving enemy fire and utterly worn down by the effort.

sentences.zh: 延通曰：「主上勤勞若此，而吾輩日享安樂。」

translations.literal: Yantong said, "Our lord toils like this, yet we daily enjoy ease and pleasure."
translations.idiomatic: Yantong said, "Our lord labors like this, while we enjoy ease every day."

sentences.zh: 蓋言不自安也。

translations.literal: This was evidently speaking of his own unease.
translations.idiomatic: —he meant that he himself felt uneasy about it.

sentences.zh: 德裕不答。

translations.literal: Deyu did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Deyu made no reply.

sentences.zh: 會張嶼先歸闕，太祖賜予甚厚。

translations.literal: When Zhang Yu first returned to court, Taizu bestowed gifts very generously.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yu returned to court first, Taizu rewarded him lavishly.

sentences.zh: 延通、德裕繼至，則召延通顧問，而待德裕稍薄。

translations.literal: When Yantong and Deyu arrived afterward, he summoned Yantong for consultation while treating Deyu somewhat more thinly.
translations.idiomatic: When Yantong and Deyu arrived afterward, Taizu summoned Yantong for consultation while treating Deyu with noticeably less favor.

sentences.zh: 德裕頗疑懼，遂奏延通嘗對眾言涉指斥，且多不法事，指嶼為黨。

translations.literal: Deyu was quite suspicious and fearful and therefore memorialized that Yantong had once spoken before the multitude in terms touching on denunciation, and moreover had many unlawful affairs, naming Yu as his faction.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed and fearful, Deyu memorialized that Yantong had once spoken seditiously before the troops and had committed numerous illegal acts, naming Yu as his accomplice.

sentences.zh: 太祖怒，即收延通、張嶼及王班下御史臺鞫之，延通等引伏。

translations.literal: Taizu was angry and immediately seized Yantong, Zhang Yu, and Wang Ban and sent them down to the Censorate for examination; Yantong and the others confessed.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu was enraged and had Yantong, Zhang Yu, and Wang Ban arrested and interrogated by the Censorate; they confessed.

sentences.zh: 太祖始欲捨之，及引問，延通抗對不遜，遂斬之。

translations.literal: Taizu at first wished to spare them, but when they were brought for questioning Yantong answered defiantly without deference, and he was therefore beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu had initially intended to spare them, but when Yantong was brought for questioning he answered defiantly and disrespectfully, and was executed.

sentences.zh: 嶼、班並內臣王仁吉並仗脊，嶼配流沙門島，班許州，仁吉西窯務，時開寶二年也。

translations.literal: Yu, Ban, and inner attendant Wang Renji were all beaten on the back; Yu was assigned to Liushamen Island, Ban to Xuzhou, Renji to the Western Kiln Office—this was in the second year of Kaibao.
translations.idiomatic: Yu, Ban, and inner attendant Wang Renji were flogged; Yu was exiled to Liushamen Island, Ban to Xuzhou, and Renji to the Western Kiln Office—in the second year of Kaibao.

sentences.zh: 梁迥，博州聊城人。

translations.literal: Liang Jiong, a native of Liaocheng in Bozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Jiong was a native of Liaocheng in Bozhou.

sentences.zh: 少為吏部小史。

translations.literal: In youth he was a junior clerk in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he served as a junior clerk in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 周世宗在藩邸日，得給事左右。

translations.literal: When Zhou Shizong was in his princely residence, he came to serve at his side.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong of Later Zhou was still a prince, Jiong came to serve in his household.

sentences.zh: 及嗣位，補殿直，改供奉官，四遷至左藏庫使。

translations.literal: When he succeeded to the throne, Jiong was given supplemental appointment as palace guard, changed to palace attendant, and through four promotions reached Left Treasury commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong succeeded to the throne, Jiong was appointed palace guard, then palace attendant, and rose through four promotions to commissioner of the Left Treasury.

sentences.zh: 太祖將討西蜀，以迥監秦州戍兵。

translations.literal: When Taizu was about to campaign against Western Shu, Jiong was made overseer of Qinzhou garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu prepared to campaign against Western Shu, Jiong was placed in charge of the garrison at Qinzhou.

sentences.zh: 蜀平，改監霸州兵，轉宮苑使。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified, he was changed to oversee Bazhou troops and transferred to Palace Parks commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu was pacified he was reassigned to oversee troops at Bazhou and then promoted to commissioner of the Palace Parks.

sentences.zh: 從征太原還，會命蜀州刺史聶章為沁州兵馬部署，以迥監其軍。

translations.literal: Returning from the Taiyuan campaign, it happened that Shuzhou prefect Nie Zhang was appointed Qinzhou army deployment commissioner, and Jiong was made overseer of his army.
translations.idiomatic: On returning from the Taiyuan campaign, when Shuzhou prefect Nie Zhang was appointed deployment commissioner for Qinzhou, Jiong was assigned to supervise his army.

sentences.zh: 無何，幷人入寇，迥與閻彥進同率兵擊敗之，以功遷東上閤門使。

translations.literal: Before long the Bing people invaded; Jiong together with Yan Yanjin led troops and defeated them, and for merit was moved to Eastern Upper Gate commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Bing forces invaded; Jiong and Yan Yanjin led troops to defeat them, and he was promoted to Eastern Upper Gate commissioner for his service.

sentences.zh: 開寶五年，命為廣南道兵馬都監兼諸州巡檢。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Kaibao he was ordered as Guangnandao army cavalry and infantry overseer and concurrently inspector of various prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Kaibao he was appointed overseer of cavalry and infantry on the Guangnan route and concurrent inspector of the prefectures in that region.

sentences.zh: 八年，奉使江南。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was sent on mission to Jiangnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was sent on a mission to Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 迥素貪冒，外務矯飾，初若嚴毅不可犯，雖饋食亦不受，江南人頗憚之。

translations.literal: Jiong was by nature greedy and reckless; outwardly he cultivated display, at first seeming stern and unapproachable, refusing even offered food, and the Jiangnan people were quite in awe of him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong had always been greedy and grasping; outwardly he affected austerity, at first seeming stern and unapproachable and refusing even gifts of food, so the people of Jiangnan were much in awe of him.

sentences.zh: 既而奉以貲貨，殆直數萬緡，迥即大喜過望，登舟縱酒，繼日宴樂。

translations.literal: Thereafter they presented goods and wealth worth nearly tens of thousands of strings of cash; Jiong was immediately delighted beyond expectation, boarded his boat and gave himself to wine, feasting day after day.
translations.idiomatic: But when they presented him with goods worth nearly ten thousand strings of cash, he was overjoyed, boarded his boat, and gave himself to wine and feasting for days on end.

sentences.zh: 及歸，戀戀不發，人多笑之。

translations.literal: When he returned he lingered unwilling to depart, and many people laughed at him.
translations.idiomatic: When it was time to return he lingered reluctantly, and many people laughed at him.

sentences.zh: 暨王師伐金陵，命迥與潘美、劉遇率步兵先赴荊南。

translations.literal: When the imperial army attacked Jinling, Jiong was ordered with Pan Mei and Liu Yu to lead infantry first to Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army marched on Jinling, Jiong was ordered to join Pan Mei and Liu Yu in leading infantry ahead to Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 且以迥護行營步兵及左廂戰棹，與吳人戰采石，殺獲甚眾。

translations.literal: Moreover Jiong was assigned to protect the campaign infantry and the left wing war boats; fighting the Wu people at Caishi, he killed and captured a great multitude.
translations.idiomatic: He was also assigned to protect the campaign infantry and the left-wing war boats; at Caishi he fought the Wu forces and killed or captured a great many of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 江南平，以功領順州團練使。

translations.literal: When Jiangnan was pacified, for merit he headed Shunzhou regimentation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After Jiangnan was pacified he was made regimentation commissioner of Shunzhou for his service.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，判四方館事，領禁軍戍澤州。

translations.literal: When Taizong took the throne, he judged Sifang Guan affairs and headed the forbidden army garrison at Zezhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong acceded, Jiong was placed in charge of the Office of Foreign Affairs while commanding the imperial guard garrison at Zezhou.

sentences.zh: 太平興國三年，錢俶來朝，命往淮、泗迎勞。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiping Xingguo, when Qian Chu came to court, he was ordered to go to Huai and Si to welcome and comfort him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taiping Xingguo, when Qian Chu came to court, Jiong was sent to the Huai and Si region to welcome and entertain him.

sentences.zh: 夏，汴水大決，詔迥發畿內丁男三千護塞汴口。

translations.literal: In summer the Bian River burst its banks on a great scale; an edict ordered Jiong to mobilize three thousand adult males from within the capital region to protect and block the Bian mouth.
translations.idiomatic: That summer the Bian River burst its banks; Jiong was ordered to mobilize three thousand men from the capital region to reinforce the breach at the river mouth.

sentences.zh: 四年，征太原，以迥為行營前軍馬步軍都監，督軍攻城，中流矢四。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, campaigning against Taiyuan, Jiong was made vanguard campaign army cavalry and infantry overseer, supervised troops in storming the city, and was struck by four arrows.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, during the campaign against Taiyuan, he served as overseer of the vanguard cavalry and infantry, directed the assault on the city, and was struck by four arrows.

sentences.zh: 車駕還，命與孟玄哲、崔翰率兵屯定州，以功遷引進使。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned, he was ordered with Meng Xuanzhe and Cui Han to lead troops stationed at Dingzhou, and for merit was moved to Reception commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor returned, he was ordered to join Meng Xuanzhe and Cui Han in garrisoning Dingzhou, and was promoted to Reception commissioner for his service.

sentences.zh: 五年，受詔與潘美城幷州於三交，及築緣邊堡障。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he received orders with Pan Mei to fortify Bingzhou at Sanjiao and to build frontier stockades and barriers.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he was ordered to join Pan Mei in fortifying Bingzhou at Sanjiao and in building frontier fortifications.

sentences.zh: 七年，李繼遷寇邊，以迥領兵護銀、夏州。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Li Jiqian raided the frontier; Jiong was made to lead troops protecting Yin and Xia prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, when Li Jiqian raided the frontier, Jiong was sent to lead troops in defense of Yin and Xia prefectures.

sentences.zh: 八年，召歸，授唐州防禦使，令赴職。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was recalled, granted Tangzhou defense commissioner, and ordered to take up his post.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was recalled and appointed defense commissioner of Tangzhou with orders to take up his post.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，繼遷誘殺都巡檢使曹光實，乘勢數寇邊。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi, Jiqian lured and killed chief inspector Cao Guangshi and seized the momentum to raid the frontier repeatedly.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongxi, Li Jiqian lured and killed chief inspector Cao Guangshi and took advantage of the situation to raid the frontier repeatedly.

sentences.zh: 復召迥為銀、夏都巡檢使，赴邊捍禦之。

translations.literal: Jiong was again summoned as Yin and Xia chief inspector and sent to the frontier to defend against him.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong was again summoned and appointed chief inspector of Yin and Xia prefectures and sent to the frontier to repel him.

sentences.zh: 三年夏，卒於銀州官舍，年五十九。

translations.literal: In summer of the third year he died at the Yinzhou official residence, aged fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the summer of the third year at the official residence in Yinzhou, at the age of fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 迥性粗率，尤不喜文士，故事，節帥出鎮及來朝，便殿宴勞，翰林學士皆預坐。

translations.literal: Jiong's nature was coarse and blunt; he especially disliked literary gentlemen. By precedent, when military commissioners went out to their commands or came to court, they were feasted and comforted in the informal hall, and Hanlin academicians all took part in seating.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong was blunt and rough by nature and especially disliked literary men. By precedent, when military commissioners departed for their commands or came to court, they were entertained in the informal hall, and Hanlin academicians were always seated among the guests.

sentences.zh: 開寶中，迥為閤門使，白太祖曰：「陛下宴犒將帥，安用此輩預坐？」

translations.literal: In Kaibao, when Jiong was gate commissioner, he told Taizu, saying, "Your Majesty feasts and rewards generals—what need is there for these fellows to take part in seating?"
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaibao reign, when Jiong was a gate commissioner, he told Taizu, "When Your Majesty feasts and rewards generals, why should these fellows be seated with them?"

sentences.zh: 自是罷之。

translations.literal: From then on this was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the practice was discontinued.

sentences.zh: 至淳化中，翰林學士蘇易簡白於太宗，始復預焉。

translations.literal: By Chunhua, Hanlin academician Su Yijian informed Taizong, and they first resumed taking part.
translations.idiomatic: In the Chunhua reign Hanlin academician Su Yijian appealed to Taizong, and the practice was restored.

sentences.zh: 大中祥符八年，錄迥子廷翰為奉職。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Dazhong Xiangfu his son Tinghan was recorded and appointed attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Dazhong Xiangfu his son Tinghan was granted appointment as an attendant.

sentences.zh: 史珪，河南洛陽人。

translations.literal: Shi Gui, a native of Luoyang in Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Gui was a native of Luoyang in Henan.

sentences.zh: 父暉，晉嚴衛指揮使。

translations.literal: His father Hui was Jin Yanwei commandant.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shi Hui had been commandant of the Jin Yanwei Guard.

sentences.zh: 珪少以武勇隸軍籍，周顯德中，遷小校。

translations.literal: Gui in youth by martial valor entered military registers; in Zhou Xiande he was moved to junior officer.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth Gui entered the army rolls for his martial prowess; during the Later Zhou Xiande reign he was promoted to junior officer.

sentences.zh: 太祖領禁衛，以珪給事左右。

translations.literal: When Taizu headed the forbidden guard, Gui was employed to serve at his side.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu commanded the imperial guard, Gui served in his personal entourage.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，用為御馬直隊長，四遷馬步軍副都軍頭兼控鶴、弓弩、大劍都指揮使。

translations.literal: When he received the abdication, Gui was employed as Imperial Horse Guard squad leader, and through four promotions became Cavalry and Infantry deputy commander-in-chief and concurrently commander of the Crane Control, Bow and Crossbow, and Great Sword commands.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took the throne, Gui was made squad leader of the Imperial Horse Guard and rose through four promotions to deputy commander-in-chief of the Cavalry and Infantry Army while concurrently commanding the Crane Control, Bow and Crossbow, and Great Sword units.

sentences.zh: 開寶六年，加都軍頭，領毅州刺史。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Kaibao he was added commander-in-chief and headed Yizhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year of Kaibao he was promoted to commander-in-chief and appointed prefect of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 太祖初臨御，欲周知外事，令珪博訪。

translations.literal: When Taizu first assumed rule, wishing to know thoroughly external affairs, he ordered Gui to make broad inquiries.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu first took the throne, wishing to learn all he could about affairs beyond the court, he ordered Gui to conduct wide-ranging inquiries.

sentences.zh: 珪廉得數事白於上，驗之皆實，由是信之，後乃漸肆威福。

translations.literal: Gui investigated and obtained several matters which he reported to the throne; on verification all were true, and thereby he was trusted; afterward he gradually indulged in power and favor.
translations.idiomatic: Gui uncovered several matters and reported them to the throne; when investigated, all proved true, and the emperor came to trust him—but Gui gradually began to abuse his influence.

sentences.zh: 民有市官物不當價者，珪告其欺罔，當置法，列肆無不側目。

translations.literal: When commoners sold government goods at improper prices, Gui reported their deception and that they should be punished by law; in the market rows none failed to cast sidelong glances.
translations.idiomatic: When commoners sold government goods at improper prices, Gui denounced them for fraud and demanded legal punishment, and every shop in the market watched in alarm.

sentences.zh: 上聞之，因下詔曰：「古人以獄市為寄者，蓋知小民唯利是從，不可盡法而繩之也。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard of it, he therefore issued an edict saying, "The ancients who entrusted the prison and market did so because they knew the common people follow profit alone and cannot all be bound by exhaustive law.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard of this he issued an edict: "The ancients who 'entrusted' the courts and markets to officials understood that common people follow profit and cannot all be prosecuted to the full extent of the law.

sentences.zh: 況先甲之令，未嘗申明。

translations.literal: Moreover the prior command had never been made clear.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the prior regulations had never been clearly announced.

sentences.zh: 苟陷人於刑，深非理道。

translations.literal: If one traps people in punishment, this deeply violates the way of principle.
translations.idiomatic: To punish people under such circumstances would be deeply unjust.

sentences.zh: 將禁其二價，宜示以明文，自今應市易官物，有妄增價直欺罔官錢者，案鞫得實，並以枉法論。

translations.literal: To forbid their double pricing, it is fitting to display written clarity: from now on in all trading of government goods, those who recklessly raise prices to deceive and cheat government funds—when investigation and examination obtain the facts—shall all be judged by the statute on perverting the law.
translations.idiomatic: To prohibit overcharging, the rules should be set out in writing: from now on, anyone who fraudulently inflates the price when trading in government goods shall, once the facts are established through investigation, be prosecuted under the statute on perverting the law.

sentences.zh: 其犯在詔前者，一切不問。」

translations.literal: Those whose offenses occurred before the edict shall all go unquestioned."
translations.idiomatic: Offenses committed before this edict shall not be prosecuted."

sentences.zh: 自是珪不復敢言。

translations.literal: From then on Gui no longer dared to speak.
translations.idiomatic: From then on Gui no longer dared to raise such matters.

sentences.zh: 時德州刺史郭貴知邢州，國子監丞梁夢昇知德州，貴族人親吏之在德州者頗為姦利，夢昇以法繩之。

translations.literal: At that time Dezhou prefect Guo Gui was administering Xingzhou; Directorate of Education aide Liang Mengsheng was administering Dezhou; Gui's clansmen and personal clerks in Dezhou were quite engaged in illicit profit, and Mengsheng bound them by law.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Dezhou prefect Guo Gui was serving as acting prefect of Xingzhou, while Directorate of Education aide Liang Mengsheng governed Dezhou; Guo's kinsmen and personal clerks in Dezhou were engaged in corrupt dealings, and Mengsheng restrained them by law.

sentences.zh: 貴素與珪善，遣人以其事告珪，圖去夢昇。

translations.literal: Guo had long been on good terms with Gui and sent someone to report the matter to Gui, plotting to remove Mengsheng.
translations.idiomatic: Guo had long been friendly with Shi Gui and sent someone to report the affair to him, hoping to have Mengsheng removed.

sentences.zh: 珪悉記於紙，將伺便言之。

translations.literal: Gui fully recorded it on paper and intended to seize a convenient moment to speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: Gui wrote everything down and waited for a suitable moment to bring it up.

sentences.zh: 一日，上因言：「爾來中外所任，皆得其人。」

translations.literal: One day the emperor remarked in passing, "Of late those appointed within and without have all obtained the right men."
translations.idiomatic: One day the emperor remarked, "Of late all appointments at court and in the provinces have been well chosen."

sentences.zh: 珪遽曰：「今之文臣，亦未必皆善。」

translations.literal: Gui hastily said, "Today's civil officials are also not necessarily all good."
translations.idiomatic: Gui quickly interjected, "Today's civil officials are not necessarily all worthy either."

sentences.zh: 乃探懷中所記以進，曰：「秖如知德州梁夢昇欺蔑刺史郭貴，幾至於死。」

translations.literal: He then drew out what he had recorded in his bosom and presented it, saying, "Take only Dezhou administrator Liang Mengsheng, who insulted and despised prefect Guo Gui, nearly to the point of death."
translations.idiomatic: He then produced the notes from his sleeve and said, "Take, for example, Dezhou administrator Liang Mengsheng, who insulted and humiliated Prefect Guo Gui almost to the point of killing him."

sentences.zh: 上曰：「此必刺史所為不法。

translations.literal: The emperor said, "This must be that the prefect acted unlawfully.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "This must mean the prefect himself acted unlawfully.

sentences.zh: 夢昇，真清強吏也。」

translations.literal: Mengsheng is a truly upright and forceful official."
translations.idiomatic: Mengsheng is a truly upright and forceful official."

sentences.zh: 因以所記紙付中書曰：「即以夢昇為贊善大夫。」

translations.literal: He thereupon handed the recorded paper to the Secretariat, saying, "Immediately make Mengsheng Assistant in the Palace Library."
translations.idiomatic: He then handed the paper to the Secretariat and said, "Appoint Mengsheng immediately as Assistant in the Palace Library."

sentences.zh: 既又曰：「與左贊善。」

translations.literal: Then he again said, "Grant Left Assistant."
translations.idiomatic: Then he added, "Make it Left Assistant."

sentences.zh: 珪以譖不行，居常怏怏。

translations.literal: Because Gui's slander did not succeed, he was habitually discontent.
translations.idiomatic: When Gui's slander failed, he remained chronically resentful.

sentences.zh: 九年，坐漏泄禁中語，出為光州刺史。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, for the offense of leaking forbidden-palace speech, he went out as Guangzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was demoted to prefect of Guangzhou for leaking palace secrets.

sentences.zh: 會歲饑，淮、蔡民流入州境，珪不待聞，即開倉減價以糶，所全活甚眾，吏民詣闕請植碑頌德者數百人。

translations.literal: It happened that the year had famine; people of Huai and Cai flowed into the prefecture's territory. Without waiting to hear from above, Gui immediately opened the granaries and sold grain at reduced prices; those he wholly preserved alive were very many. Officials and commoners who went to the court to request erecting a stele praising his virtue numbered several hundred.
translations.idiomatic: When famine struck, refugees from Huai and Cai poured into his prefecture. Without waiting for orders from the capital, Gui opened the granaries and sold grain at reduced prices, saving a great many lives. Several hundred officials and commoners went to court to ask that a stele be erected in praise of his virtue.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，以為揚、楚等九州都巡檢使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo, he was appointed chief inspector of Yang, Chu, and nine other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taiping Xingguo reign he was made chief inspector of Yang, Chu, and nine other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 四年，征太原，命珪與彰信軍節度劉遇攻城北面。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, on the campaign against Taiyuan, Gui was ordered together with Zhangxin Army military commissioner Liu Yu to attack the north side of the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, during the campaign against Taiyuan, he and Liu Yu, military commissioner of the Zhangxin Army, were ordered to assault the northern wall of the city.

sentences.zh: 從征幽州，坐所部逗撓失律，責授定武行軍司馬。

translations.literal: He followed the campaign against Youzhou; for his unit's delay and failure in discipline he was punished and appointed Dingwu campaign army vice marshal.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against Youzhou his unit was found guilty of delay and dereliction of duty, and he was demoted to vice marshal of the Dingwu campaign army.

sentences.zh: 數月，召為右衛將軍、領平州刺史。

translations.literal: After several months he was summoned as Right Guard general and concurrently Pingzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: A few months later he was recalled to serve as general of the Right Guard and concurrently prefect of Pingzhou.

sentences.zh: 督浚惠民河，自尉氏達京九十里，數旬而畢，民咸便之。

translations.literal: He supervised dredging the Huimin River from Weishi to the capital for ninety li; in several ten-day periods it was completed, and the people all found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised dredging the Huimin Canal from Weishi to the capital—a distance of ninety li—and finished the work within a few weeks, to the great benefit of the local population.

sentences.zh: 會江、淮民麹謀首等數十百人聚為盜，命珪率龍猛騎兵五百往捕，悉獲之。

translations.literal: It happened that several tens or hundreds of people from Jiang and Huai, including Qu Mou and others, gathered as bandits; Gui was ordered to lead five hundred Dragon Fierce cavalry to capture them, and all were taken.
translations.idiomatic: When several dozen people from the Jianghuai region, led by Qu Mou, banded together as outlaws, Gui was ordered to take five hundred Dragon Fierce cavalrymen after them and captured them all.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷隰州刺史，知保州、靜戎軍。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was moved to Xizhou prefect and administered Baozhou and the Jingrong Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was transferred to prefect of Xizhou and placed in charge of Baozhou and the Jingrong garrison.

sentences.zh: 上緣邊便宜十五事，皆從之。

translations.literal: He submitted fifteen expedient proposals for the frontier; all were adopted.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted fifteen practical recommendations for frontier administration, and the emperor approved every one.

sentences.zh: 雍熙中，從曹彬征幽州，為押陣部署，以所部下涿州。

translations.literal: During Yongxi he followed Cao Bin on the campaign against Youzhou as battle-line deployment commissioner and led his troops down to Zhuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongxi reign he joined Cao Bin's campaign against Youzhou as battle-line deployment commissioner and marched his command as far as Zhuozhou.

sentences.zh: 師還，卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: When the army returned he died, aged sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died after the army returned, at the age of sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 珪多智數，好以甘言小惠取譽於人，故所至不忍其去云。

translations.literal: Gui had many stratagems and liked to use sweet words and small favors to win praise from people; therefore wherever he went they could not bear to see him leave.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was resourceful and fond of winning favor with flattering words and small kindnesses, so wherever he served the people were loath to see him go.

sentences.zh: 田欽祚

translations.literal: Tian Qinzuo
translations.idiomatic: Tian Qinzuo

sentences.zh: 田欽祚，潁州汝陰人。

translations.literal: Tian Qinzuo, a native of Ruyin in Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Qinzuo was a native of Ruyin in Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 父令方，漢虢州團練使。

translations.literal: His father Lingfang was Han Guozhou regimentation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His father Tian Lingfang had been regimentation commissioner of Guozhou under the Later Han.

sentences.zh: 帳下伶人靖邊庭妻有美色，令方私之，邊庭不勝忿。

translations.literal: The wife of Jing Bianting, a performer under his command, was beautiful; Lingfang had a secret affair with her, and Bianting could not contain his rage.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Bianting, a performer in Lingfang's household, had a beautiful wife whom Lingfang seduced; Bianting was consumed with rage.

sentences.zh: 會陝西三叛連衡，關輔間人情大擾。

translations.literal: It happened that the three rebels of Shaanxi allied together, and sentiment throughout the Guanfu region was greatly disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the three rebel leaders of Shaanxi had joined forces, and public feeling throughout the Guanzhong region was in turmoil.

sentences.zh: 邊庭率其徒數人夜縋入州廨，害令方，因掠郡民投趙思綰，至潼關，與守關使者戰，遂敗散。

translations.literal: Bianting led several followers by night on ropes into the prefectural yamen, killed Lingfang, plundered county people, and went over to Zhao Sixuan; reaching Tong Pass they fought the pass defenders and were defeated and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Bianting led a handful of followers who lowered themselves by rope into the prefectural office at night, murdered Lingfang, plundered the local population, and fled to join Zhao Sixuan. At Tong Pass they fought the garrison and were routed.

sentences.zh: 朝廷錄欽祚為殿直，改供奉官。

translations.literal: The court recorded Qinzuo as palace attendant and changed his appointment to palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted Qinzuo appointment as a palace attendant and soon promoted him to palace attendant of the inner service.

sentences.zh: 周世宗征淮南，為前軍都監。

translations.literal: When Zhou Shizong campaigned against Huainan, he served as vanguard army overseer.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizong campaigned against Huainan, Qinzuo served as overseer of the vanguard army.

sentences.zh: 從征關南還，會塞澶淵決河，命欽祚領禁兵護役，因令督治澶州城。

translations.literal: Returning from the Guannan campaign, when the breach at Chentyuan on the Yellow River was being sealed he was ordered to lead forbidden troops to protect the laborers and was also charged with supervising repair of Cangzhou city.
translations.idiomatic: After the Guannan campaign he returned just as work began to close a Yellow River breach at Chentyuan. Qinzuo was ordered to lead imperial troops to guard the project and to supervise repairs to the walls of Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 淮人寇高密，刺史王萬威求濟師，命欽祚領州兵援之，既至，圍解。

translations.literal: Huai people raided Gaomi; prefect Wang Wanwei requested relief troops. Qinzuo was ordered to lead prefectural troops to aid him, and once he arrived the siege was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: When raiders from the Huai region attacked Gaomi, Prefect Wang Wanwei asked for reinforcements. Qinzuo was sent with local troops to relieve the city, and the siege was broken as soon as he arrived.

sentences.zh: 宋初，遷閤門通事舍人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song he was moved to gate communications attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Song dynasty he was promoted to communications attendant of the Inner Gate Office.

sentences.zh: 乾德二年冬，討蜀，為北路先鋒都監，令乘傳往來宣達機事。

translations.literal: In the winter of the second year of Qiande, on the campaign against Shu, he was northern-route vanguard overseer and was ordered to ride post relays back and forth conveying strategic affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the second year of Qiande, during the Shu campaign, he served as overseer of the northern-route vanguard and was charged with riding the post roads to convey military intelligence.

sentences.zh: 孟昶降，奉捷書馳奏，遷西上閤門副使。

translations.literal: When Meng Chang surrendered, he presented the victory report by rapid dispatch and was moved to Western Upper Gate deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Meng Chang surrendered he raced back with the victory report and was promoted to Western Upper Gate deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 蜀土寇亂，又遣欽祚率師討平之。

translations.literal: Shu territory had bandit turmoil, and Qinzuo was again sent to lead troops to pacify it.
translations.idiomatic: When banditry broke out across Shu, he was again sent to lead troops and put the disturbances down.

sentences.zh: 四年春，幷人寇樂平，從羅彥瓌拒之，獨以所部三千人破寇，擒副將一人，俘獲甚眾，以功遷西上閤門使。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourth year, Bing people raided Leping; he followed Luo Yanrang to resist them and alone with his three thousand troops broke the raiders, captured one deputy general, and took very many prisoners; for merit he was moved to Western Upper Gate commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourth year, when forces from Bing raided Leping, he joined Luo Yanrang in the defense and, with only his own three thousand men, routed the enemy, captured a deputy commander, and took a large number of prisoners. For this he was promoted to Western Upper Gate commissioner.

sentences.zh: 開寶二年，又與何繼筠破賊兵於石嶺關，領賀州刺史，判四方館使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kaibao he again with He Jiyun broke the bandit army at Shiling Pass, held Hezhou prefect, and judged Sifang Guan affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Kaibao he and He Jiyun again defeated rebel forces at Shiling Pass. He was then made prefect of Hezhou and placed in charge of the Office for Tributary Affairs.

sentences.zh: 三年，契丹寇中山，以欽祚為定州路兵馬都部署。

translations.literal: In the third year, when the Khitan raided Zhongshan, Qinzuo was made Dingzhou route army deployment commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, when Khitan forces raided Zhongshan, he was appointed overall deployment commissioner for military affairs on the Dingzhou route.

sentences.zh: 與戰遂城，自旦及晡，殺傷甚眾。

translations.literal: He fought at Suicheng from dawn until afternoon; the killed and wounded were very many.
translations.idiomatic: He fought at Suicheng from dawn until late afternoon, and casualties on both sides were heavy.

sentences.zh: 欽祚馬中流矢踣，騎士王超授欽祚以馬，軍復振，敵解去。

translations.literal: Qinzuo's horse was struck by a flying arrow and fell; cavalryman Wang Chao gave Qinzuo his horse, the army revived, and the enemy withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Qinzuo's horse was hit by an arrow and collapsed, but the cavalryman Wang Chao gave him his own mount. The army rallied and the enemy withdrew.

sentences.zh: 朝廷將議討江表，遣欽祚覘之，還奏合旨，江南所得寶貨直三千萬，悉以賜欽祚。

translations.literal: The court was about to discuss campaigning against Jiangbiao and sent Qinzuo to reconnoiter; his report on return accorded with the emperor's intent, and treasures taken from Jiangnan worth thirty million were all given to Qinzuo.
translations.idiomatic: As the court prepared to discuss a campaign against the lower Yangzi region, Qinzuo was sent to reconnoiter. His report pleased the emperor, and the entire thirty-million-worth of treasure seized in Jiangnan was given to him.

sentences.zh: 會興師，首命欽祚與曹彬、李漢瓊率騎軍先赴江陵，就命為昇州西南路行營馬軍兼左廂戰棹都監。

translations.literal: When the army was raised, Qinzuo was first ordered with Cao Bin and Li Hanqiong to lead the cavalry to Jiangling first, and concurrently appointed Xingzhou Southwest Route campaign cavalry army and left-wing battle-boat overseer.
translations.idiomatic: When war was declared he was among the first ordered, with Cao Bin and Li Hanqiong, to lead the cavalry to Jiangling. At the same time he was made overseer of cavalry on the Xingzhou Southwest Route campaign staff and of the left-wing battle fleet.

sentences.zh: 領兵敗吳軍萬餘於溧水，斬其主帥李雄等五人，擒裨將二人。

translations.literal: Leading troops he defeated more than ten thousand Wu troops at Lishui, beheaded their commander Li Xiong and four others—five in all—and captured two deputy generals.
translations.idiomatic: He led his troops to defeat more than ten thousand Wu soldiers at Lishui, beheaded the enemy commander Li Xiong and four other senior officers, and captured two deputy commanders.

sentences.zh: 進圍金陵，為南面攻城部署。

translations.literal: He advanced to besiege Jinling as southern siege deployment commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed on to besiege Jinling as deployment commissioner for the southern assault.

sentences.zh: 既平，以功加領汾州防禦使。

translations.literal: After pacification, for merit he was additionally granted Fenzhou defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After the region was pacified he was additionally made defense commissioner of Fenzhou for his service.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，遷引進使，為晉州都鈐轄。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo he was moved to Reception commissioner and made Jinzhou chief regimentation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taiping Xingguo reign he was promoted to Reception commissioner and appointed chief regimentation commissioner of Jinzhou.

sentences.zh: 太原驍將楊業率眾寇洪洞縣，欽祚擊敗之，斬首千餘級，獲馬數百。

translations.literal: Taiyuan's fierce general Yang Ye led troops to raid Hongdong County; Qinzuo defeated him, beheaded more than a thousand, and captured several hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Ye, a formidable Taiyuan commander, led a raid against Hongdong County, Qinzuo routed him, took more than a thousand heads, and seized several hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 太宗賜欽祚白金五千兩，令市宅。

translations.literal: Taizong bestowed on Qinzuo five thousand taels of white gold and ordered him to buy a residence.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong rewarded him with five thousand taels of silver and told him to purchase a house.

sentences.zh: 四年，從征太原，護前鋒騎兵，屯石嶺關以扞契丹。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he followed the Taiyuan campaign, escorted the vanguard cavalry, and encamped at Shiling Pass to block the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he joined the Taiyuan campaign, escorted the vanguard cavalry, and held Shiling Pass to block the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 欽祚性剛戾負氣，多所忤犯，與主帥郭進不協，進戰功高，屢為欽祚所陵，心不能甘，遂自縊死。

translations.literal: Qinzuo's nature was harsh, arrogant, and proud; he often gave offense. He did not get along with commander Guo Jin. Jin's battle merit was high, yet he was repeatedly humiliated by Qinzuo; unable to accept this, he hanged himself.
translations.idiomatic: Qinzuo was harsh, arrogant, and quick to give offense. He clashed with his commander Guo Jin, a man of distinguished battle record whom Qinzuo repeatedly humiliated until Jin, unable to bear the shame, hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 初，賊兵奄至，進出戰，欽祚但閉壁自守，既去，又不追。
