translations.literal: At first, when the bandit army suddenly arrived, Jin went out to fight while Qinzuo only closed the walls and defended himself; after they left he did not pursue.
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion, when enemy troops suddenly appeared, Jin went out to fight while Qinzuo merely shut the gates and held the walls; after the enemy withdrew he made no attempt to pursue.

sentences.zh: 所受月奉芻粟，多販鬻規利，為部下所訴，責授睦州團練使。

translations.literal: Much of the monthly salary fodder and grain he received he sold for profit; subordinates complained, and he was punished and appointed Muzhou regimentation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He was reported by his subordinates for selling off much of the fodder and grain issued as his monthly stipend for private profit, and was demoted to regimentation commissioner of Muzhou.

sentences.zh: 車駕北巡，以為幽州西路行營壕砦都監。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage toured the north, he was made Youzhou Western Route campaign trench-and-fort overseer.
translations.idiomatic: During the emperor's northern tour he was appointed overseer of trenches and fortifications on the western wing of the Youzhou campaign staff.

sentences.zh: 六年秋，改房州團練使，逾年，又改柳州。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the sixth year he was changed to Fangzhou regimentation commissioner; after more than a year he was again changed to Liuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of the sixth year he was transferred to regimentation commissioner of Fangzhou, and a year later was moved to Liuzhou.

sentences.zh: 嶺外多瘴氣，因遘疾，累表乞生還闕下。

translations.literal: Beyond the Lingnan passes miasma was abundant; he therefore fell ill and repeatedly memorialized begging to return alive to the court.
translations.idiomatic: The malarial air of the far south made him ill, and he repeatedly petitioned to be allowed to return alive to the capital.

sentences.zh: 上憐之，遷郢州團練使。

translations.literal: The emperor pitied him and moved him to Yingzhou regimentation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took pity on him and transferred him to regimentation commissioner of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 在郡二年，入覲，欽祚見上，涕泣不已。

translations.literal: After two years in the prefecture he entered audience; Qinzuo saw the emperor and wept without stopping.
translations.idiomatic: After two years in office he came to court for an audience and wept continuously before the emperor.

sentences.zh: 以為銀、夏、綏、宥都巡檢使，俄召還。

translations.literal: He was made chief inspector of Yin, Xia, Sui, and You, and soon summoned back.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed chief inspector of Yin, Xia, Sui, and You, and was soon recalled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 會征幽州，命欽祚與宣徽南院使郭守文為排陣使。

translations.literal: When the Youzhou campaign was launched, Qinzuo was ordered together with Southern Bureau Palace Secretariat commissioner Guo Shouwen to serve as battle-array commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign against Youzhou was ordered, he and Guo Shouwen, commissioner of the Southern Bureau of the Palace Secretariat, were appointed battle-array commissioners.

sentences.zh: 時欽祚已被病，受詔不勝喜，一夕，卒。

translations.literal: At that time Qinzuo was already ill; receiving the edict he was overcome with joy, and one night later he died.
translations.idiomatic: By then Qinzuo was already ill. Overjoyed at receiving the order, he died that very night.

sentences.zh: 欽祚性陰狡，尤不喜儒士，好狎侮同列，人多惡之。

translations.literal: Qinzuo's nature was secretive and cunning; he especially disliked Confucian scholars and liked to mock and insult colleagues, and many hated him.
translations.idiomatic: Qinzuo was secretive and cunning, had little use for scholars, and delighted in belittling his peers; he was widely disliked.

sentences.zh: 子承誨，仕至供奉官、閤門祗候；

translations.literal: His son Chenghui served up to palace attendant and gate usher.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chenghui rose to the posts of palace attendant and gate usher.

sentences.zh: 承說，至崇儀副使。

translations.literal: Chengshuo reached Honored Ceremonial deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chengshuo rose to Honored Ceremonial deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 侯贇，幷州太原人。

translations.literal: Hou Yun, a native of Taiyuan in Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Yun was a native of Taiyuan in Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 父義，漢遼州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Yi was Han Liaozhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hou Yi had been prefect of Liaozhou under the Later Han.

sentences.zh: 贇以蔭補殿前承旨。

translations.literal: Yun by yin privilege was given supplemental appointment as Palace Front attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Yun entered service through his father's privilege as an attendant of the Palace Front Office.

sentences.zh: 周顯德中，再遷至供奉官，使江南，復命領三門、集津發運使。

translations.literal: During Zhou Xiande he was twice promoted to palace attendant, served as envoy to Jiangnan, and on return to duty was ordered to head the Sanmen and Jijin transport commission.
translations.idiomatic: During the Later Zhou Xiande reign he was promoted twice to palace attendant, served as envoy to Jiangnan, and on his return was put in charge of transport at Sanmen and Jijin.

sentences.zh: 王文寶

translations.literal: Wang Wenbao
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wenbao

sentences.zh: 王文寶，開封陽武人，以任子補殿直。

translations.literal: Wang Wenbao, a native of Yangwu in Kaifeng, by sons-of-officials privilege was given supplemental appointment as palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wenbao was a native of Yangwu in Kaifeng and entered service as a palace attendant through the privilege granted to officials' sons.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，累遷至軍器庫使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo he was repeatedly promoted to Armory commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taiping Xingguo reign he rose through successive promotions to commissioner of the Armory.

sentences.zh: 嘗使契丹。

translations.literal: He once served as envoy to the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: He once served as envoy to the Khitan.

sentences.zh: 會陳洪進獻漳、泉地，以文寶監泉州兵。

translations.literal: When Chen Hongjin offered the Zhang and Quan territories, Wenbao was made supervisor of Quanzhou troops.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen Hongjin surrendered Zhang and Quan, Wenbao was assigned to supervise the troops at Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 群盜大起，文寶與轉運使楊克讓、知州喬惟岳共討平之。

translations.literal: Bandits rose in great numbers; Wenbao together with transport commissioner Yang Kerang and prefect Qiao Weiyue jointly campaigned and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: When banditry erupted on a large scale, Wenbao joined Transport Commissioner Yang Kerang and Prefect Qiao Weiyue in suppressing the uprising.

sentences.zh: 以功領媯州刺史，加內弓箭庫使。

translations.literal: For merit he additionally held Guizhou prefect and was given the post of Inner Bow and Crossbow Armory commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made prefect of Guizhou and additionally appointed commissioner of the Inner Bow and Crossbow Armory.

sentences.zh: 二年，京西轉運使程能議開新河，自襄、漢至京師，引白河水注焉，以通湘、潭之漕。

translations.literal: In the second year, Jingxi transport commissioner Cheng Neng proposed opening a new canal from Xiang and Han to the capital, diverting Bai River water into it to connect Xiang and Tan grain transport.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, Jingxi Transport Commissioner Cheng Neng proposed digging a new canal from Xiangyang and Hanzhong to the capital, feeding it with water from the Bai River to link the grain routes of Xiang and Tan to the capital.

sentences.zh: 詔發唐、鄧、汝、潁、許、蔡、陳、鄭丁夫數萬赴其役，又發諸州兵萬人助之。

translations.literal: An edict mobilized tens of thousands of corvee laborers from Tang, Deng, Ru, Ying, Xu, Cai, Chen, and Zheng for the work, and also mobilized ten thousand troops from various prefectures to assist.
translations.idiomatic: An edict called up tens of thousands of corvée laborers from Tang, Deng, Ru, Ying, Xu, Cai, Chen, and Zheng, and ten thousand troops from various prefectures were also sent to help.

sentences.zh: 命文寶與六宅使李繼隆、作坊副使李仁祐、劉承珪分往護作。

translations.literal: Wenbao was ordered together with Six Residences commissioner Li Jilong, workshop deputy commissioner Li Renyou, and Liu Chenggui to go separately to supervise the work.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbao was ordered to join Li Jilong, commissioner of the Six Residences Office, Workshop Deputy Commissioner Li Renyou, and Liu Chenggui in supervising separate sections of the project.

sentences.zh: 既而地高水下，不能通，卒堙廢焉。

translations.literal: Before long the land was high and the water low, so it could not connect; in the end it was filled in and abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The terrain proved too high for the water to flow through, the canal never connected, and the project was finally filled in and abandoned.

sentences.zh: 雍熙四年，改東上閤門使，歷知涇、延二州。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yongxi he was changed to Eastern Upper Gate commissioner and successively administered Jing and Yan prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yongxi he was made Eastern Upper Gate commissioner and served in succession as prefect of Jing and Yan.

sentences.zh: 會遼人寇通遠軍，命文寶率師致討，還遷判四方館事。

translations.literal: When Liao people raided Tongyuan Army, Wenbao was ordered to lead troops to punish them; on return he was moved to judge Sifang Guan affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Liao forces attacked Tongyuan Army, Wenbao was ordered to lead a punitive expedition, and on his return was promoted to head the Office for Tributary Affairs.

sentences.zh: 文寶歷內職三十年，雅好言外事，太祖、太宗頗信任之，中外咸畏其口。

translations.literal: Wenbao held inner posts for thirty years, was fond of speaking on foreign affairs, and Taizu and Taizong quite trusted him; inside and outside the court all feared his mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Wenbao spent thirty years in palace service, was fond of discussing foreign affairs, and enjoyed considerable trust from both Taizu and Taizong; officials at court and beyond feared what he might say.

sentences.zh: 出為高陽關兵馬鈐轄，淳化二年，卒於官。

translations.literal: He went out as Gaoyang Pass army regimentation commissioner; in the second year of Chunhua he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as regimentation commissioner of the forces at Gaoyang Pass and died in office in the second year of Chunhua.

sentences.zh: 翟守素

translations.literal: Di Shousu
translations.idiomatic: Di Shousu

sentences.zh: 翟守素，濟州任城人。

translations.literal: Di Shousu, a native of Rencheng in Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Di Shousu was a native of Rencheng in Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 父溥，晉左司禦率府率。

translations.literal: His father Pu was Jin Left Palace Guard chamberlain of the commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Di Pu had been chamberlain of the Left Palace Guard under the Jin.

sentences.zh: 守素以父任為殿直，曆漢、周，遷供奉官，領承天軍使。

translations.literal: Shousu by his father's appointment was palace attendant; through Han and Zhou he was promoted to palace attendant and headed the Chengtian Army commission.
translations.idiomatic: Shousu entered service as a palace attendant through his father's privilege, served through the Later Han and Later Zhou, was promoted to palace attendant, and commanded the Chengtian Army.

sentences.zh: 乾德中，為引進副使，從王全斌伐蜀，以往來馳告軍事為職。

translations.literal: During Qiande he was Reception deputy commissioner; following Wang Quanbin against Shu, his duty was riding back and forth to report military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qiande reign he served as Reception deputy commissioner on Wang Quanbin's Shu campaign, charged with riding the post roads to convey military reports.

sentences.zh: 蜀平，擢判四方館事。

translations.literal: When Shu was pacified he was promoted to judge Sifang Guan affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Shu was pacified he was promoted to head the Office for Tributary Affairs.

sentences.zh: 以兩川餘寇未殄，慮致騷動，再令守素入蜀經略諸郡，分兵以防遏之。

translations.literal: Because remnant bandits in the Two Rivers had not been exterminated and unrest was feared, Shousu was again ordered into Shu to manage the various prefectures and divide troops to guard against them.
translations.idiomatic: Because bandit remnants in the Two Rivers region had not yet been eliminated and might stir unrest, Shousu was again sent into Shu to oversee the prefectures and garrison troops to contain them.

sentences.zh: 開寶中，會麟、府內屬戎人爭地不決，因致擾亂，命守素馳往撫喻。

translations.literal: During Kaibao, when subordinate tribes of Lin and Fu disputed land without resolution and thereby caused disturbance, Shousu was ordered to rush there to pacify and instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaibao reign, when affiliated tribal peoples of Lin and Fu fell into dispute over land and the quarrel turned violent, Shousu was ordered to go at once and settle the matter.

sentences.zh: 守素辨其曲直，戎人悅服。

translations.literal: Shousu distinguished right and wrong among them, and the tribes submitted gladly.
translations.idiomatic: Shousu judged the rights and wrongs of the case, and the tribes accepted his ruling with satisfaction.

sentences.zh: 從征太原，命海州刺史孫方進圍汾州，守素監其軍，轉引進使。

translations.literal: On the Taiyuan campaign he was ordered that Haizhou prefect Sun Fangjin besiege Fenzhou; Shousu supervised his army and was transferred to Reception commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On the Taiyuan campaign he supervised the forces of Sun Fangjin, prefect of Haizhou, in the siege of Fenzhou, and was then promoted to Reception commissioner.

sentences.zh: 開寶三年，命為劍南十州都巡檢使，東上閣門使郭崇信副之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Kaibao he was appointed chief inspector of ten Jiannan prefectures, with Eastern Upper Gate commissioner Guo Chongxin as deputy.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Kaibao he was made chief inspector of ten prefectures in Jiannan, with Guo Chongxin, Eastern Upper Gate commissioner, as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 賜守素錢五百萬，入謝日，復遣為岐帥符彥卿官告使。

translations.literal: Shousu was granted five million cash; on the day he entered to give thanks he was again sent as credential envoy for Qizhou military commissioner Fu Yanqing.
translations.idiomatic: The court granted him five million cash, and on the day he came to give thanks he was again dispatched as credential envoy to Fu Yanqing, military commissioner of Qi.

sentences.zh: 守素辭以錫齎優厚，不敢更當奉使之詔，上不許。

translations.literal: Shousu declined on the grounds that the gift was too generous and he dared not accept another envoy edict; the emperor did not permit this.
translations.idiomatic: Shousu declined, saying the reward was already more than generous and he did not dare accept another envoy appointment, but the emperor would not hear of it.

sentences.zh: 九年，吳越國王錢俶來朝，命守素護諸司供帳，迎勞郊外。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, when Wuyue king Qian Chu came to court, Shousu was ordered to oversee the various offices' supplies and tents and welcome and honor him outside the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, when King Qian Chu of Wuyue came to court, Shousu was ordered to supervise the provisioning of the visit and to welcome him outside the city.

sentences.zh: 並壘未下，詔與洺州防禦使郭進率兵深入其境，蹈藉禾稼，守素多所虜獲。

translations.literal: The Taiyuan fortresses had not yet fallen; an edict ordered him together with Mingzhou defense commissioner Guo Jin to lead troops deep into enemy territory, trample the grain crops, and Shousu captured much booty.
translations.idiomatic: While the Taiyuan fortresses still held out, he and Guo Jin, defense commissioner of Mingzhou, were ordered to lead a deep raid into enemy territory, trampling the crops; Shousu brought back a large haul of captives and plunder.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，遷客省使，領憲州刺史。

translations.literal: When Taizong succeeded to the throne, Shousu was moved to guest-relations commissioner and held Xianzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong took the throne, Shousu was promoted to guest-relations commissioner and made prefect of Xianzhou.

sentences.zh: 太平興國三年夏，河決滎陽，詔守素發鄭之丁夫千五百人，與卒千人領護塞之。

translations.literal: In the summer of the third year of Taiping Xingguo the Yellow River breached at Xingyang; an edict ordered Shousu to mobilize fifteen hundred corvee laborers from Zheng together with one thousand soldiers to oversee blocking it.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the third year of Taiping Xingguo the Yellow River broke its banks at Xingyang, and Shousu was ordered to mobilize fifteen hundred corvée laborers from Zheng and a thousand soldiers to supervise the repair.

sentences.zh: 是秋，梅山洞蠻恃險叛命，詔遣守素率諸州屯兵往擊之。

translations.literal: That autumn the Meishan cave barbarians, relying on difficult terrain, rebelled against orders; an edict sent Shousu to lead garrison troops from various prefectures to attack them.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn the Meishan cave tribes rebelled, trusting in their rugged terrain, and Shousu was ordered to lead garrison troops from several prefectures against them.

sentences.zh: 值霖雨彌旬，弓弩解弛，不堪用，明日，將接戰，守素一夕令削木為弩。

translations.literal: Continuous rain lasted more than ten days; bows and crossbows loosened and could not be used. The next day battle was about to be joined, and in one night Shousu ordered wood carved into crossbows.
translations.idiomatic: After more than ten days of steady rain their bows and crossbows had warped and were useless. On the eve of battle Shousu had his men carve wooden crossbows in a single night.

sentences.zh: 及旦，賊奄至，交射之，賊遂敗。

translations.literal: At dawn the bandits suddenly arrived; both sides exchanged shots, and the bandits were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn the rebels attacked without warning; both sides exchanged volleys, and the rebels were routed.

sentences.zh: 乘勝逐北，盡平其巢穴。

translations.literal: Riding victory he pursued north and completely pacified their nests.
translations.idiomatic: He pressed the victory, pursued the fleeing enemy, and wiped out their strongholds entirely.

sentences.zh: 先是，數郡大吏、富人多與賊帥包漢陽交通，既而得其書訊數百封，守素並焚之，反側以定。

translations.literal: Previously many great officials and wealthy people of several prefectures had communicated with bandit leader Bao Hanyang; afterward several hundred of their letters were obtained, and Shousu burned them all, so unrest was settled.
translations.idiomatic: Many senior officials and wealthy men in several prefectures had been in contact with the rebel leader Bao Hanyang. When several hundred of their letters were seized, Shousu burned them all, and the region settled down.

sentences.zh: 俄而錢俶獻浙右之地，詔守素為兩浙諸州兵馬都監，安撫諸郡，人心甚悅，即以知杭州。

translations.literal: Soon Qian Chu offered the Zheyou territories; an edict made Shousu overall army overseer of the Liangzhe prefectures to pacify the various prefectures. People's hearts were very pleased, and he was immediately made prefect of Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Qian Chu surrendered the lands of western Zhejiang. Shousu was appointed overall military overseer of the Liangzhe prefectures to pacify the region, won wide approval, and was immediately made prefect of Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 歲滿，為西京巡檢使。

translations.literal: When his term was complete he was made Western Capital inspector commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired he was appointed inspector commissioner of the Western Capital.

sentences.zh: 秦王廷美以事勒歸私第，以守素權知河南府兼留守司事，屬洛陽歲旱艱食，多盜，上憂之。

translations.literal: Prince of Qin Tingmei was compelled by an affair to return to his private residence; Shousu was made acting Henan prefect and concurrently in charge of the capital-guard commissioner's office. Luoyang that year had drought and scarce food and many bandits, and the emperor was worried.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Tingmei of Qin was forced to retire to his private residence, Shousu was made acting prefect of Henan and placed in charge of the capital-guard commissioner's office. Luoyang was suffering drought, food was scarce, and banditry was rife, and the emperor was deeply concerned.

sentences.zh: 守素既至，漸以寧息。

translations.literal: Once Shousu arrived, things gradually became peaceful and quiet.
translations.idiomatic: After Shousu took up his post, order was gradually restored.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷商州團練使。

translations.literal: Before long he was moved to Shangzhou regimentation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was transferred to regimentation commissioner of Shangzhou.

sentences.zh: 雍熙二年，改知延州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongxi he was changed to administer Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongxi he was appointed administrator of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 自劉廷讓敗於君子館，河朔諸州城壘多圮。

translations.literal: Since Liu Tingrang was defeated at Junzi Lodge, the city walls and ramparts of the Hebei prefectures were largely ruined.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Tingrang's defeat at Junzi Lodge, the fortifications of the Hebei prefectures lay largely in ruins.

sentences.zh: 四年，詔守素與田仁朗、王繼恩、郭延濬分路按行，發諸州鎮兵增築，護其役。

translations.literal: In the fourth year an edict ordered Shousu together with Tian Renlang, Wang Jien, and Guo Yanjun to travel by separate routes to inspect, mobilize garrison troops of the various prefectures to augment construction, and oversee the labor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Shousu was ordered, together with Tian Renlang, Wang Jien, and Guo Yanjun, to tour the region by separate routes, mobilize garrison troops from the prefectures to rebuild the walls, and supervise the work.

sentences.zh: 賜白金三十兩，留充天雄軍兵馬鈐轄、知大名府，改知潞州。

translations.literal: He was granted thirty taels of white gold, retained as Tianxiong Army army overseer and administrator of Daming prefecture, then changed to administer Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He received thirty taels of white gold, was retained as army overseer of the Tianxiong Army and administrator of Daming prefecture, and later transferred to administer Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 會建方田，命為代北方田都部署、并州兵馬鈐轄，從屯夏州，改知鳳翔府。

translations.literal: When the square-field system was established, he was ordered as northern field overall deployment commissioner for Dai and Bingzhou army overseer; he followed in garrison at Xiazhou and was changed to administer Fengxiang prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When the square-field system was introduced he was appointed overall deployment commissioner for the northern fields and army overseer of Bingzhou, garrisoned at Xiazhou, and later made administrator of Fengxiang prefecture.

sentences.zh: 淳化中，夏帥趙保忠上言，其弟繼遷誘戎人為寇，且求援師。

translations.literal: In Chunhua, Xia commander Zhao Baozhong submitted a report that his younger brother Jiqian was inducing the Rong people to raid and also requested relief troops.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chunhua reign the Xia commander Zhao Baozhong reported that his younger brother Jiqian was inciting the tribes to raid and asked for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 詔守素率兵復屯夏州，未幾，又徙石州，以老病上疏求歸本郡，從之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Shousu to lead troops again to garrison Xiazhou; before long he was again moved to Shizhou; because of age and illness he submitted a memorial requesting return to his home commandery, and this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Shousu was ordered to lead troops back to garrison Xiazhou; soon afterward he was transferred to Shizhou, and citing age and illness he memorialized to return to his home region, which was granted.

sentences.zh: 三年，卒，年七十一。

translations.literal: In the third year he died, aged seventy-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third year, at the age of seventy-one.

sentences.zh: 守素逮事四朝，綿歷內職五十餘年。

translations.literal: Shousu reached through service to four courts and continuously held inner-office posts for more than fifty years.
translations.idiomatic: Shousu served four successive dynasties and held palace appointments for more than fifty years.

sentences.zh: 性謹慎，寬仁容眾，所至有治績。

translations.literal: His nature was cautious and prudent, generous and tolerant toward the multitude; wherever he went there were records of good governance.
translations.idiomatic: He was cautious by nature, generous and tolerant of others, and left a record of effective governance wherever he served.

sentences.zh: 凡斷大辟獄，雖罪狀明白，仍遍詢僚寀，僉同而後決；

translations.literal: Whenever he decided capital cases, even when the criminal facts were clear, he still broadly questioned his staff officers and only decided after unanimous agreement;
translations.idiomatic: In every capital case, even when the facts were clear, he would consult all his staff and proceed only after unanimous agreement;

sentences.zh: 屬吏有過不麵折，必因公宴援往事之相類者言其獲咎，以微警之。

translations.literal: when subordinate officials had faults he did not rebuke them to their faces but invariably at public banquets cited analogous past cases of those who had suffered blame, to give them a subtle warning.
translations.idiomatic: when a subordinate erred he never rebuked him to his face but at a public banquet would cite a similar past case in which someone had been punished, as a subtle warning.

sentences.zh: 新進後生多至節帥，而守素久次不遷，殊無隕獲意，時論以此多之。

translations.literal: Newly advanced younger men often reached military commissioner rank, yet Shousu for long tenure was not promoted and had not the slightest sense of dejection; contemporary opinion greatly praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Many younger men rose to military commissioner rank while Shousu remained long in place without promotion, yet he showed no resentment; public opinion greatly admired him for it.

sentences.zh: 王侁，字秘權，開封浚儀人。

translations.literal: Wang Shen, courtesy name Miquan, a native of Junyi in Kaifeng.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shen, whose courtesy name was Miquan, came from Junyi in Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 父樸，周樞密使，侁以父任太仆寺丞。

translations.literal: His father Pu was Zhou Privy Councilor; Shen entered office through his father as Grand Stud vice director.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wang Pu had been Privy Councilor under the Later Zhou; Shen received appointment as vice director of the Grand Stud through his father's privilege.

sentences.zh: 樸卒，世宗幸其第，召見諸孤，以侁為東頭供奉官。

translations.literal: When Pu died, Shizong visited his residence, summoned and saw the orphans, and made Shen Eastern Head palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When Pu died, Shizong visited his home, received his orphaned sons, and appointed Shen Eastern Head palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 開寶中，征江南，命侁率師戍桐城。

translations.literal: In Kaibao, on the campaign against Jiangnan, Shen was ordered to lead troops to garrison Tongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaibao campaign against Jiangnan he was ordered to lead troops in garrison at Tongcheng.

sentences.zh: 王師渡江，與樊若水同知池州，領兵敗江南軍四千餘於宣州。

translations.literal: When the imperial army crossed the Yangzi, he together with Fan Ruoshui jointly administered Chizhou and led troops to defeat more than four thousand Jiangnan troops at Xuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial army crossed the Yangzi he served with Fan Ruoshui as joint administrator of Chizhou and defeated more than four thousand Jiangnan troops at Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 金陵平，加閣門祗候。

translations.literal: When Jinling was pacified he was added as gate attendant.
translations.idiomatic: After Jinling fell he was promoted to gate attendant.

sentences.zh: 太平興國初，預討梅山洞蠻。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiping Xingguo he took part in suppressing the Meishan cave barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taiping Xingguo reign he took part in suppressing the Meishan cave tribes.

sentences.zh: 契丹使來貢，詔侁送於境上。

translations.literal: When Khitan envoys came to offer tribute, an edict ordered Shen to escort them to the border.
translations.idiomatic: When Khitan tribute envoys arrived, Shen was ordered to escort them to the frontier.

sentences.zh: 還，使靈州、通遠軍。

translations.literal: On his return he was envoy to Lingzhou and Tongyuan Army.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was sent on missions to Lingzhou and the Tongyuan Army.

sentences.zh: 及旋，言主帥所留牙兵率與邊人交結，頗桀黠難製，歲久當慮，請悉代之。

translations.literal: When he returned he said that the military adjutants left by commanders mostly formed ties with frontier people, were quite fierce and cunning and hard to control, and that after many years this should be a concern; he requested that they all be replaced.
translations.idiomatic: On returning he reported that the adjutants left behind by frontier commanders had largely formed ties with local tribes, were fierce and unruly, and that after long service they posed a risk; he asked that they all be replaced.

sentences.zh: 太宗因遣侁調內郡卒往代之。

translations.literal: Taizong thereupon sent Shen to transfer troops from inner prefectures to replace them.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong accordingly sent Shen to bring in troops from the interior prefectures to replace them.

sentences.zh: 戍者聞代，多不願還。

translations.literal: The garrison troops hearing of replacement mostly did not wish to return.
translations.idiomatic: When the garrison troops learned they were to be replaced, most were unwilling to return.

sentences.zh: 侁察其中旅拒者斬之以徇，眾皆悚息，遂將以還。

translations.literal: Shen detected those among them who resisted travel and beheaded them as a warning; the multitude all trembled into silence, and he thereupon led them back.
translations.idiomatic: Shen identified those who resisted and executed them as an example; the rest were cowed into submission, and he led them back.

sentences.zh: 一歲中數往來西邊，多奏便宜，上多聽用，遷通事舍人。

translations.literal: Within one year he traveled back and forth to the western frontier several times, submitted many expedient proposals, and the emperor mostly adopted them; he was moved to communications attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Within a year he made several trips to the western frontier, submitted numerous practical proposals that the emperor largely adopted, and was promoted to communications attendant.

sentences.zh: 四年，從征太原，以侁護陽曲、塌地、石嶺關諸屯，賜廄馬介胄。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he followed the campaign against Taiyuan; Shen was assigned to protect the garrisons at Yangqu, Tadi, and Shiling Pass, and was granted stable horses and armor.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, during the campaign against Taiyuan, he was assigned to protect the garrisons at Yangqu, Tadi, and Shiling Pass and was granted horses and armor from the imperial stables.

sentences.zh: 五月，即城下轉東上閣門副使。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, right at the foot of the city he was transferred to Eastern Upper Gate deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, while still at the city walls, he was promoted to Eastern Upper Gate deputy commissioner.

sentences.zh: 晉陽平，留為嵐、憲巡檢。

translations.literal: When Jinyang was pacified he was retained as inspector of Lan and Xian.
translations.idiomatic: After Jinyang fell he was left behind as inspector of Lan and Xian prefectures.

sentences.zh: 九年，代還，遷西上閣門使，賜錢百萬。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, when his replacement returned, he was moved to Western Upper Gate commissioner and granted a million in cash.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, when his tour ended, he was promoted to Western Upper Gate commissioner and granted one million in cash.

sentences.zh: 河西三族首領折遇乜叛入李繼遷，侁帥師討擒之，以功領蔚州刺史。

translations.literal: The Hexi Three Clans leader Zhe Yuye rebelled and entered Li Jiqian's service; Shen led troops to campaign against and capture him, and for merit headed Youzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Zhe Yuye, leader of the Hexi Three Clans, rebelled and joined Li Jiqian; Shen led troops to capture him and was appointed prefect of Youzhou for his service.

sentences.zh: 王師北征，命為并州駐泊都監，又為雲、應等州兵馬都監。

translations.literal: When the imperial army campaigned north, he was ordered as Bingzhou garrison overseer and also as Yun, Ying, and other prefectures army overseer.
translations.idiomatic: During the northern campaign he was appointed garrison overseer at Bingzhou and also army overseer for Yun, Ying, and related prefectures.

sentences.zh: 侁性剛愎，以語激楊業，業因力戰陷於陣，侁坐除名，配隸金州，事載《楊業傳》。

translations.literal: Shen's nature was stubborn and self-willed; with words he provoked Yang Ye, and Ye therefore fought fiercely and fell in battle; Shen was punished by removal from the registers and assigned to serve Jinzhou—the affair is recorded in the 《Biography of Yang Ye》.
translations.idiomatic: Shen was obstinate and headstrong; he goaded Yang Ye with his words, and Ye fought to the death and fell in battle. Shen was stripped of his rank and assigned to Jinzhou; the affair is recorded in the 《Biography of Yang Ye》.

sentences.zh: 會赦，移均州團練副使。

translations.literal: When an amnesty occurred he was moved to Junzhou regimentation deputy commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After an amnesty he was transferred to deputy regimentation commissioner of Junzhou.

sentences.zh: 淳化五年召還，道病，至京師卒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Chunhua he was summoned back; he fell ill on the road and died on reaching the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Chunhua he was recalled to court, fell ill on the journey, and died after reaching the capital.

sentences.zh: 弟僎，供奉官、閤門祗候，坐征交阯軍敗誅；

translations.literal: His younger brother Zhuan was palace attendant and gate attendant; for the offense of defeat in the campaign against Jiaozhi he was executed;
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zhuan, a palace attendant and gate attendant, was executed for the defeat of the army in the campaign against Jiaozhi;

sentences.zh: 備、偃並進士及第，偃至太常博士。

translations.literal: Bei and Yan both passed the jinshi examination; Yan reached Doctor of the Grand Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Bei and Yan both passed the jinshi examination; Yan rose to Doctor of the Grand Temple.

sentences.zh: 樸弟格，宋初為右補闕、直史館，至都官員外郎、廣南轉運使。

translations.literal: Pu's younger brother Ge, at the beginning of Song was Right Remonstrator and direct historian of the Historiography Institute, reaching Ministry of Justice external bureau director and Guangnan transport commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Pu's younger brother Ge served early in the Song as Right Remonstrator and direct historian of the Historiography Institute, and rose to external bureau director of the Ministry of Justice and transport commissioner of Guangnan.

sentences.zh: 格子侗，太平興國進士，至都官員外郎。

translations.literal: Ge's son Tong was a Taiping Xingguo jinshi and reached Ministry of Justice external bureau director.
translations.idiomatic: Ge's son Tong passed the jinshi examination in the Taiping Xingguo reign and rose to external bureau director of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 劉審瓊

translations.literal: Liu Shenqiong
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shenqiong

sentences.zh: 劉審瓊，涿州范陽人。

translations.literal: Liu Shenqiong, a native of Fanyang in Zhuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shenqiong was a native of Fanyang in Zhuozhou.

sentences.zh: 家素貧。

translations.literal: His family was by nature poor.
translations.idiomatic: His family had always been poor.

sentences.zh: 漢乾祐中，湘陰公鎮彭門，審瓊始隸帳下。

translations.literal: In Han Qianyou the Prince of Xiangyin garrisoned Pengmen; Shenqiong first entered service under his command.
translations.idiomatic: During the Later Han Qianyou reign, when the Prince of Xiangyin held Pengmen, Shenqiong first entered his service.

sentences.zh: 周祖受命，遁去，依永興軍節度劉詞，頗委任之。

translations.literal: When Zhou Taizu received the Mandate he fled away and attached himself to Yongxing Army military commissioner Liu Ci, who greatly entrusted affairs to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhou Taizu seized power he left that service and attached himself to Liu Ci, military commissioner of the Yongxing Army, who entrusted him with considerable responsibility.

sentences.zh: 詞卒，屬太祖節鎮，給事左右。

translations.literal: When Ci died he came under Taizu's military commission and served at his side.
translations.idiomatic: After Liu Ci died he entered the service of Taizu, then a military commissioner, and attended him personally.

sentences.zh: 及受禪，補殿直。

translations.literal: When Taizu received the abdication he was given supplemental appointment as palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu took the throne he was appointed palace guard.

sentences.zh: 從平澤、潞，改供奉官。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying Ze and Lu and was changed to palace attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the pacification of Ze and Lu prefectures and was promoted to palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 開寶中，累遷至軍器庫使。

translations.literal: In Kaibao he was repeatedly promoted to Arsenal commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaibao reign he rose in succession to commissioner of the Arsenal.

sentences.zh: 會樞密使李崇矩門人鄭伸擊登聞鼓，誣告崇矩受太原席羲叟黃金，私結翰林學士扈蒙，以甲科私羲叟，引審瓊為證。

translations.literal: It happened that Privy Councilor Li Chongju's follower Zheng Shen struck the Denunciation Drum, falsely accusing Chongju of receiving gold from Taiyuan's Xi Aisou, privately associating with Hanlin academician Hu Meng to favor Aisou with top examination rank, and citing Shenqiong as witness.
translations.idiomatic: Li Chongju's follower Zheng Shen struck the Denunciation Drum and falsely accused Chongju of accepting gold from Xi Aisou of Taiyuan and colluding with Hanlin academician Hu Meng to award Aisou the top examination rank, naming Shenqiong as a witness.

sentences.zh: 上怒，召審瓊詰問，審瓊具言其誣枉，得解，遂出知鎮州。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and summoned Shenqiong to interrogate him; Shenqiong fully stated the false accusation, the case was resolved, and he then went out to administer Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was furious and summoned Shenqiong for questioning; Shenqiong fully exposed the false accusation, the case was dropped, and he was sent out as prefect of Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 七年，太宗征河東，駐蹕月餘，儲㣥無闕，遷領檀州刺史、知潭州。

translations.literal: In the seventh year Taizong campaigned against Hedong and halted his progress for more than a month; stores were without lack, and he was moved to head Tanzhou prefect while administering Chizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year, when Taizong campaigned against Hedong and halted for more than a month, Shenqiong supplied the army without shortfall and was promoted to prefect of Tanzhou while serving as administrator of Chizhou.

sentences.zh: 州素多火，日調民積水為防，民甚勞之。

translations.literal: The prefecture had always had many fires; daily the people were mobilized to store water as prevention, and the people were greatly burdened.
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture had long suffered frequent fires, and the people were daily mobilized to store water as a precaution, which imposed a heavy burden on them.

sentences.zh: 審瓊至，悉罷之，以為民便。

translations.literal: When Shenqiong arrived he abolished all of it, considering it a convenience for the people.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenqiong arrived he abolished the practice entirely, to the great relief of the people.

sentences.zh: 徙知河陽。

translations.literal: He was transferred to administer Heyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as administrator of Heyang.

sentences.zh: 淳化三年，受代歸，陳衰老，乞正受郡符。

translations.literal: In the third year of Chunhua, when his replacement arrived he returned, stated his old age, and requested formal receipt of a prefectural commission.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Chunhua, when his successor arrived, he returned to court, cited his advanced age, and asked for a formal prefectural appointment.

sentences.zh: 上閔其舊人，授坊州刺史。

translations.literal: The emperor pitied him as an old companion and granted him Fangzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor, pitying an old companion, appointed him prefect of Fangzhou.

sentences.zh: 至道三年，卒於官。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhidao he died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He died in office in the third year of Zhidao.

sentences.zh: 審瓊嘗給事外諸侯，雅善酒令博鞠，年八十餘，筋力不衰，髭髮黳黑。

translations.literal: Shenqiong had once served outer feudal lords and was by nature skilled at wine commands, gambling, and cuju; past eighty years his sinew and strength did not decline, and his beard and hair were dark black.
translations.idiomatic: Shenqiong had once served various regional lords and was adept at drinking games, gambling, and cuju; even past eighty his strength did not fail him, and his beard and hair remained dark.

sentences.zh: 孫爽，進士及第，後為祠部員外郎、秘閣校理。

translations.literal: His grandson Shuang passed the jinshi examination and later served as Ministry of Rites external bureau director and Secretariat collator.
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Shuang passed the jinshi examination and later served as external bureau director of the Ministry of Rites and collator of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 論曰：王贊奮跡小校，有奉公之節，繩姦列郡，不畏強禦。

translations.literal: Discussion says: Wang Zan rose from traces as a junior officer, had the integrity of serving the public, restrained the wicked in successive prefectures, and did not fear the powerful.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: Wang Zan rose from the ranks as a junior officer, upheld the duty of public service, restrained wrongdoing across the prefectures he governed, and did not flinch before the powerful.

sentences.zh: 保續單車出使，不辱君命。

translations.literal: Baoxu went out alone in a single carriage as envoy and did not dishonor his lord's charge.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Baoxu traveled alone on diplomatic missions and never failed in his charge.

sentences.zh: 懷忠識荊渚之將危。

translations.literal: Huaizhong recognized that Jingzhu was about to be imperiled.
translations.idiomatic: Lu Huaizhong foresaw the imminent peril of Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 繼勳知番禺之可取。

translations.literal: Jixun knew that Panyu could be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jixun saw that Panyu could be conquered.

sentences.zh: 侯贇久治邊郡。

translations.literal: Hou Yun for long governed frontier prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Yun long administered the frontier prefectures.

sentences.zh: 文寶數護屯兵：斯各一時之效也。

translations.literal: Wenbao repeatedly protected garrison troops: these were each the effect of a single time.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wenbao repeatedly oversaw frontier garrisons—these were each timely contributions in their own way.

sentences.zh: 德裕、梁迥、欽祚、王侁皆練習戎旅，頗著勳勞，然率強戾而乏溫克，以速於戾，斯乃明哲之所戒。

translations.literal: Deyu, Jiong, Qinzuo, and Wang Shen all were practiced in military campaigns and showed considerable merit and toil, yet they were by nature forceful and harsh and lacked gentle restraint; by hastening to harshness, this is what the wise and perspicacious warn against.
translations.idiomatic: Ding Deyu, Liang Jiong, Tian Qinzuo, and Wang Shen were all seasoned in military affairs and won considerable distinction, yet they were habitually harsh and lacked self-restraint; to rush into violence is what the wise counsel against.

sentences.zh: 比以剛險蒙悔吝，珪以發擿肆威福，其不逞者歟！

translations.literal: By comparison, for stubborn treachery they met regret and distress; Gui by exposing and denouncing indulged in power and favor—were these not the unbridled!
translations.idiomatic: The former group met disgrace through stubborn treachery; Shi Gui abused his power through denunciation and exposure—were these not men who could not contain themselves!

sentences.zh: 守素不事躁競，審瓊克享期頤。

translations.literal: Shousu did not engage in rash competition; Shenqiong was able to enjoy a full lifespan.
translations.idiomatic: Di Shousu did not strive rashly for advancement; Liu Shenqiong lived out his full span of years.

sentences.zh: 《易》曰：「視履考祥，其旋元吉。」

translations.literal: The 《Changes》 says: "Observing the tread and examining the auspicious, on turning back there is primal good fortune."
translations.idiomatic: The 《Book of Changes》 says, "He observes his conduct and examines the omens; when he turns back, there is supreme good fortune."

sentences.zh: 此之謂也。

translations.literal: This is what is meant.
translations.idiomatic: This is what is meant.
